# Sodero Cloud

# Get Started

# Sodero Cloud Documentation

Build a simulated environment in **Studio**, configure robot software in **Stellar Station**, and view the simulation in **Theater**. Open the portal at [app.sodero.io](https://app.sodero.io).

## Start Here

1. Read [What Is Sodero Cloud](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/get_started/sodero_cloud/index.md) and [Key Concepts](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/get_started/key_concepts/index.md).
1. Follow the [Quick Start](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/get_started/quick_start/index.md) to create, view and stop your first World.
1. Configure a [Robot System](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/overview/index.md) when you are ready to connect controllers to simulated robots.

Robot Systems and Robot Worlds use credits from **Activate** to **Deactivate**, even while they are stopped ([Activate and Run](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/get_started/key_concepts/#activate-and-run)).

## Find Your Task

| Task                                   | Read                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Sign in and choose a workspace         | [Account](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/sign_in/index.md), [Workspaces](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/workspaces/index.md)                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Check credits, usage and plan limits   | [Billing and Usage](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/billing/index.md)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Create files and share a project       | [Projects](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/projects/index.md), [Systems and Worlds](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/files/index.md), [Sharing](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/sharing/index.md)                                                                               |
| Share files with everyone in a project | [Libraries](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/libraries/index.md)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Build or import a scene                | [Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/studio/index.md), [Prepare a World](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/prepare_world/index.md)                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Install apps and configure a robot     | [Apps](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/apps/index.md), [Graph](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/graph/index.md), [Documents](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/documents/index.md), [World connection](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/world_connection/index.md) |
| Run, inspect and end a session         | [Activate and Run](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/index.md), [Monitor nodes](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/run/index.md), [Theater](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/theater/index.md)                                                                             |
| Drive robots with a controller UI      | [Strider](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/strider/index.md), [Motion Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/motion_studio/index.md), [Articulation](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/articulation/index.md)                                                                       |
| Connect external tools                 | [AI Agents](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/ai_agents/index.md), [Project VPN](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/project_vpn/index.md)                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Check versions and limits              | [Compatibility](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/reference/compatibility/index.md), [Limits](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/reference/limits/index.md)                                                                                                                                                               |

## Scope

This manual covers Sodero Cloud. For physical controllers and hardware setup, use the [Stellar X manual](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/latest/). The two products run their own releases of Stellar Station, so menus, app versions and document formats can differ ([Compatibility](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/reference/compatibility/index.md)).

For help, use **Help › Contact support** in the portal or [contact Sodero](https://www.sodero.io/contact).

# What Is Sodero Cloud

Sodero Cloud runs the Sodero robot platform in your browser. You build a simulated place for your robots, compose their robot systems in Stellar Station, run both in the cloud and watch them live, with nothing to install.

______________________________________________________________________

## Projects, Worlds and Systems

Everything you build lives in a **project** in the Sodero Cloud portal at `https://app.sodero.io`. A project holds two kinds of file:

- **Robot Worlds**: simulated places with your robots in them, for example a warehouse with a mobile base.
- **Robot Systems**: the robot software. Each Robot System is one **Stellar Station**.

The Robot Systems of a project drive the robots in the project's active Robot World.

______________________________________________________________________

## Core Ideas

**Studio builds the World, the cloud simulates it, Theater shows it.** You build a Robot World in **Studio**, the World editor: bring in a scene, add robots and environments from Sodero Assets, arrange them and save. When you activate the World, Sodero Cloud simulates it. **Theater** shows the running World live in your browser, with the robots and the Stations that drive them.

**Each Robot System is a Stellar Station.** It uses a graph of nodes and Stellar Designer document types (`.gw`, `.sdd`, `.sddm`, `.sdda`). These concepts also apply to Stellar X. The available apps, menus and accepted document versions depend on the installed release ([Compatibility](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/reference/compatibility/index.md)).

**The World connects by itself.** The simulation gateways of every active Station in the project connect to the project's active World automatically. There is no Isaac Sim to install and no network to set up: each gateway finds its robot in the World by name.

______________________________________________________________________

## From Design to a Running Robot

```
flowchart TB
    D["Design<br>Stellar Designer documents"] --> W["Build the World<br>Studio"]
    W --> C["Compose<br>Stellar Station"]
    C --> R["Run and watch<br>Theater"]
    C -. ".sdr transfer:<br>check compatibility" .-> X["Stellar X<br>real hardware"]
```

**Design.** Describe each robot and its gateway in Stellar Designer documents: kinematics, wheels, limits and actuator mapping. Sodero also publishes ready-made documents in **Sodero Assets**.

**Build the World.** In [Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/studio/index.md), bring in a scene or Sodero Assets, arrange them and save. The World must follow a few rules so that Stations can drive its robots ([Prepare a World for Simulation](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/prepare_world/index.md)).

**Compose.** In the [Station](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/overview/index.md), add gateways and controllers as nodes, connect their ports and load their documents.

**Run and watch.** On the project page, activate the World and its Robot Systems and run them ([Activate and Run](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/index.md)). Watch the World in [Theater](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/theater/index.md) and operate the robots from the controller UIs ([Strider](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/strider/index.md)).

______________________________________________________________________

## Sodero Cloud and Stellar X

**Stellar X** is Sodero's motion controller for real robots. It runs the same Stellar Station on the robot, with EtherCAT for real drives ([Stellar X manual](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/latest/)).

|                            | Sodero Cloud                                       | Stellar X                                                               |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Where the Station runs     | In the cloud, one per Robot System                 | On the Stellar X controller                                             |
| What it drives             | Robots simulated in the project's Robot World      | Real drives through EtherCAT, or a robot in NVIDIA Isaac Sim on your PC |
| Simulation                 | Built in: Studio, the cloud simulation and Theater | Isaac Sim with the Isaac Bridge extension, on your PC                   |
| Save a Station to a file   | **Download local copy** (`.sdr`)                   | **Export SDR**                                                          |
| Load a Station from a file | **Import** (`.sdr`)                                | **Load SDR**                                                            |

**Move a Robot System with an `.sdr` file.** Check the destination's Station release and apps first ([Move Robot Systems Between Stellar X and Sodero Cloud](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/files/#move-robot-systems-between-stellar-x-and-sodero-cloud)).

**Adapt the design for real hardware.** Controllers send commands through a gateway. Reusing a controller design on Stellar X requires a compatible release, a hardware gateway, and checks of actuator mapping, calibration, limits and sensors. Follow the device manual before enabling motion.

**Tip:** Build and test the robot system in Sodero Cloud first. When it behaves as it should in the World, take it to the real robot on Stellar X.

______________________________________________________________________

## What You Need

| You need         | Details                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A browser        | Everything runs in the browser: the portal, Studio, the Station, the controller UIs and Theater.                                                                                                                                                    |
| A Sodero account | Sign in at `https://app.sodero.io` ([Sign In and Account](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/sign_in/index.md)).                                                                                                                    |
| Credits          | Active Robot Systems and Robot Worlds use your workspace's credits ([Billing and Usage](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/billing/index.md)).                                                                                      |
| Rendering        | **WebGPU** needs support from your browser, operating system and GPU. **RTX Real-time** renders in the cloud and streams the view to your device. See [Compatibility](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/reference/compatibility/index.md). |

______________________________________________________________________

## Find Your Way in the Portal

### The Left Navigation Bar

The left navigation bar is the column of icons on the left of every portal page.

| Item                        | Opens                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Sodero logo, **Home**       | Your **Recent** and **Favorites** projects, Robot Systems and Robot Worlds                                                                                            |
| **Projects**                | The projects of the current workspace, or your guest projects ([Projects](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/projects/index.md))                     |
| **Library**                 | The libraries of the projects in the current workspace ([Libraries](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/libraries/index.md))                          |
| **Trash**                   | Items moved to Trash in this workspace ([Projects](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/projects/#7-move-to-trash-restore-and-delete))                 |
| **Notifications**, **Help** | See below                                                                                                                                                             |
| Your avatar                 | **Account Settings**, **Sign-in & Security**, **Theme** and **Sign out** ([Sign In and Account](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/sign_in/index.md)) |

The name of the current workspace is at the top left of the page; click it for the workspace menu ([Workspaces and People](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/workspaces/index.md)).

### Notifications

Click the bell (**Notifications**) in the left navigation bar to see recent activity in the current workspace, such as projects created or trashed, people added or removed, and Robot Systems and Robot Worlds started, stopped or failed. A red badge counts the unread entries; **Read All** marks them read.

### Help and Feedback

Click **Help** in the left navigation bar. The menu has **Documentation**, **Report a bug**, **Share an idea** and **Contact support**.

The Help menu

- **Report a bug** or **Share an idea**: fill in the fields, attach up to 10 PNG, JPG or PDF files (20 MB in total) if you like, and click **Submit report** or **Submit idea**. Sodero receives it with your name, email address and account ID, the page you were on and your browser details.
- **Contact support** opens the Sodero website in a new tab.

Do not include passwords, access keys or other sensitive information in the text or in the attachments.

Continue with [Key Concepts](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/get_started/key_concepts/index.md), then try the [Quick Start](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/get_started/quick_start/index.md).

# Key Concepts

This page explains the terms you meet everywhere in Sodero Cloud: workspaces and projects, Robot Systems and Robot Worlds, activation, Studio and Theater, and the parts of a Station. Read it once before the [Quick Start](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/get_started/quick_start/index.md).

______________________________________________________________________

## Workspaces and Projects

```
flowchart TB
    subgraph WS ["Workspace: people, plan, credits"]
        subgraph P ["Project: files and the people who can open them"]
            A["Robot System A<br>Stellar Station"] -- "simulation gateway" --> W["Robot World<br>simulated in the cloud"]
            B["Robot System B<br>Stellar Station"] -- "simulation gateway" --> W
        end
    end
```

| Term             | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Workspace**    | Where a team works together: its people, its projects, its plan and its credits. You can belong to several workspaces ([Workspaces and People](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/workspaces/index.md)). |
| **Project**      | Robot Systems and Robot Worlds that belong together, and the people who can open them ([Projects](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/projects/index.md))                                                |
| **Robot System** | A project file that is one Stellar Station ("the Station"): the robot system's nodes, documents, settings and apps                                                                                                       |
| **Robot World**  | A project file that holds a simulated place: a USD scene with the ground, the lighting, objects and robots                                                                                                               |

A project can hold several Robot Worlds, but only one of them can be active at a time. Any number of Robot Systems can be active, within your plan's limit of **Systems and Worlds running at once**, and they all drive robots in that World ([How Robot Worlds and Robot Systems Work Together](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/files/#4-how-robot-worlds-and-robot-systems-work-together)).

______________________________________________________________________

## Activate and Run

Each Robot System and Robot World has its own environment in the cloud. Two columns on the project page control it, and they are separate steps:

| Column         | States                   | What it does                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Activation** | **Inactive**, **Active** | **Activate** brings the environment up: a Station restores its saved data, a World loads its saved scene. **Deactivate** releases it.            |
| **Running**    | **Stopped**, **Running** | **Run** starts what is in an active environment: the Station's nodes, the World's simulation. **Stop** stops them; the environment stays active. |

- **Credits.** An active file uses your workspace's credits for every minute it is active, whether or not anything runs in it. Stop does not end that; Deactivate does. Studio and Theater sessions can use credits too, depending on their rendering mode ([Billing and Usage](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/billing/index.md)).
- **Auto off.** An active file that nobody has used for 30 minutes is deactivated automatically, unless an editor has cleared its **Auto off** box. A Station counts as used while someone has it open or works with it through an AI agent or the Project VPN; a World, while someone watches it in Theater.

Details: [Activate and Run](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/index.md).

______________________________________________________________________

## Studio and Theater

| Tool        | For                                                                                                                                                                                  | Opens while the World is |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------ |
| **Studio**  | Building the World: bring in scenes and Sodero Assets, arrange objects, set mass and joint poses, save ([Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/studio/index.md)) | **Inactive**             |
| **Theater** | Watching the running World: select robots and see the Station that drives each one ([Theater](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/theater/index.md))                   | **Active**               |

Both ask first for a **rendering mode**. **RTX Real-time** draws the World on a cloud GPU; **WebGPU** draws it in your browser with your computer's GPU. The mode changes only how you see the World: the simulation is the same for everyone ([Choose Rendering Mode](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#choose-rendering-mode)).

______________________________________________________________________

## Inside a Robot System: the Station

A **Station** is a graph of **nodes**. Each node is one program, such as a gateway, a robot controller, a navigation component or a module of your own. **Add node** offers four types:

| Type            | Purpose                                       |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| **Gateway**     | Connects simulation or hardware to the system |
| **Controller**  | Defines a robot unit and its control          |
| **Compound**    | Combines several robot units into one system  |
| **Application** | Defines robot behaviors and task logic        |

Every node runs an **app**. Sodero's apps come from the Station's **Store**; your own module packages are added on **Modules**. A new Robot System can start with a bundle of apps, its **Starting apps** ([Apps and Packages](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/apps/index.md)).

The IDs of Sodero's nodes start with `sodero.`. Most of them end with a name you choose, usually the robot's:

| Node                                        | ID                                         |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Actuator gateway                            | `sodero.actuator_gateway.<name>`           |
| Camera gateway                              | `sodero.camera_gateway.<name>`             |
| Mobile base controller                      | `sodero.mlc.<name>`                        |
| Manipulator controller (Motion Studio)      | `sodero.mmc.<name>`                        |
| Articulated robot controller (Articulation) | `sodero.amc.<name>`                        |
| Strider, the operator UI of a mobile base   | `sodero.strider`                           |
| Localizer, Navigator                        | `sodero.icp_localizer`, `sodero.navigator` |

### Ports

Nodes work together through **ports**. Each node card lists **REQUIRES**, the services the node needs, and **PROVIDES**, the services it offers. You connect a required port to a matching provided port; the Station refuses ports that do not match. A mobile robot such as Jackal uses two connections:

```
flowchart TB
    S["Strider<br>sodero.strider"] -- "mobile_base" --> M["Mobile base controller<br>sodero.mlc.jackal"]
    M -- "servo_link" --> G["Actuator gateway<br>sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal"]
    G -- "robot name jackal" --> W["Robot World<br>robot /World/jackal"]
```

| Requires                | Provides                             | Meaning                                       |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| Controller `servo_link` | Actuator gateway `servo_link`        | The controller drives the gateway's actuators |
| Strider `mobile_base`   | Mobile base controller `mobile_base` | Strider operates this mobile base             |

See [Build the Graph](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/graph/index.md).

### Gateways and Documents

A **gateway** is the only node that talks to actuators; controllers send their commands through it. In Sodero Cloud, a simulation gateway drives a robot in the project's World. On Stellar X, an EtherCAT gateway drives real drives; the controllers work the same way, in the Station release that the device runs ([Compatibility](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/reference/compatibility/index.md)).

Gateways and controllers are configured by **design documents**, which you upload into the node's **Parameters** ([Documents and Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/documents/index.md)):

| File    | Node             | Contents                                                  |
| ------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.gw`   | Actuator gateway | Hardware type and actuators                               |
| `.sdd`  | `sodero.mmc`     | Manipulator: kinematics, dynamics, actuator mapping       |
| `.sddm` | `sodero.mlc`     | Mobile base: drive type, wheels, limits, actuator mapping |
| `.sdda` | `sodero.amc`     | Articulated robot: joints and actuator mapping            |

**Names must match.** A simulation gateway finds its robot in the World by name. The **Robot name** of the gateway node must be exactly the name of the robot's prim in the World, for example `jackal` for `/World/jackal`. With another name, the robot never moves. See [Connect to the World](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/world_connection/index.md).

______________________________________________________________________

## Glossary

| Term                  | Meaning                                                                                                           |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Workspace             | A team's space in the portal: people, projects, plan and credits                                                  |
| Project               | Robot Systems and Robot Worlds that belong together, and who can open them                                        |
| Robot System          | A project file that is one Stellar Station                                                                        |
| Stellar Station       | The application that runs a robot system as a graph of nodes. Stellar X runs it too, in the device's own release. |
| Robot World           | A project file with a simulated place and the robots in it                                                        |
| Studio                | The World editor                                                                                                  |
| Theater               | The live view of an active World                                                                                  |
| Activate, Deactivate  | Bring a file's environment up, or release it                                                                      |
| Run, Stop             | Start or stop what runs in an active environment                                                                  |
| Auto off              | Deactivates a file that nobody has used for 30 minutes                                                            |
| Credits               | What active files and rendering sessions use, from your workspace's plan                                          |
| RTX Real-time, WebGPU | The rendering modes: on a cloud GPU, or on your computer's GPU                                                    |
| Node                  | One program in the Station, such as a gateway, a controller or a module of your own                               |
| Port                  | A connection point of a node: REQUIRES (needs) or PROVIDES (offers)                                               |
| Gateway               | A node that connects controllers to actuators or sensors, simulated or real                                       |
| Controller            | A node that controls a robot unit, such as a mobile base or a manipulator                                         |
| Design document       | The configuration of a gateway or a robot controller: `.gw`, `.sdd`, `.sddm`, `.sdda`                             |
| App                   | A package from the Store that a node runs                                                                         |
| Robot name            | The name of a robot's prim in the World, set on the simulation gateway node that drives it                        |
| `.sdr`                | A Sodero file that holds one Robot System or one Robot World                                                      |
| Sodero Assets         | Robots, environments and documents published by Sodero                                                            |

# Quick Start

Create a warehouse World, watch its simulation in Theater, then stop and deactivate it. This first exercise walks through the whole life of a World; driving its robots from a Station comes next ([Next: Connect a Robot System](#next-connect-a-robot-system)).

## Before You Start

- Sign in to [Sodero Cloud](https://app.sodero.io) with access to create a project and edit its files.
- In the workspace menu, open **Billing & Usage** and check the credits left and **Systems and Worlds running at once**.
- Download [jackal_warehouse.zip](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/get_started/quick_start/files/jackal_warehouse.zip), the example scene with a Jackal and a Dingo. Keep the ZIP intact. It includes the accompanying Clearpath license notice.

**Credits:** an active World uses credits until you deactivate it, and Studio and Theater sessions can use credits while they are open. **Billing & Usage** shows your plan's rates ([Billing and Usage](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/billing/index.md)).

## Step 1: Create the Project and World

1. In **Projects**, click **+ Project**.
1. Enter `Warehouse Demo`, keep **Restricted**, and click **Create**.
1. In the project, click **New file**, choose **Robot World**, and click **Next**.
1. Enter `warehouse` as the **File Name**, then click **Create**.

Naming the new Robot World

The World appears as **Inactive**. Its **Studio** link opens the editor.

## Step 2: Import and Save the Scene

1. Click **Studio** on the World row. Choose **RTX Real-time** or **WebGPU**, then click **Open Cosmic Studio**. Studio opens in a new tab. Keep the Sodero Cloud tab open while you work: Studio uses it to keep you signed in and to read library files.

1. Open the logo menu and choose **World › Replace scene…**.

1. On **This PC**, select `jackal_warehouse.zip`, click **Replace**, and confirm replacement.

   The Replace scene dialog

1. Check that the **Hierarchy** shows `dingo_d`, `jackal` and `warehouse`.

1. Click **Save now** in the left rail and wait for *Saved just now*.

The example scene in Studio. It contains a Jackal and a Dingo.

Choose **Back to Sodero Cloud** from the logo menu to close Studio.

## Step 3: Activate the World

On the project page, set the World's **Activation** to **Active**. Wait until **Activating** changes to **Active**. Activation prepares the environment; it does not start the simulation.

## Step 4: View and Run the Simulation

1. Click **Theater**, choose a rendering mode, and click **Open Cosmic Theater**.
1. Wait for *Ready*.
1. On the project page, set the World's **Running** state to **Running**. You can also click **Start Theater** in Theater when you control it: the first person with edit access who opened Theater controls **Start Theater** and **Stop Theater** ([Start and Stop](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/theater/#start-and-stop)).
1. Select **jackal** in **Scene assets**; double-click the row to bring the camera to it.

The readout at the bottom of the viewport shows **FPS**, the rate at which your view is drawn, and **Physics RTF**, the real-time factor of the simulation: simulated time divided by wall-clock time. Near 1.00, the simulation keeps up with real time. The robots stay where they are until a Robot System drives them.

## Step 5: Stop and End the Session

1. Set the World's **Running** state to **Stopped**. Stopping resets its pose and clock; it is not a pause that preserves progress.
1. Set **Activation** to **Inactive** and wait for deactivation to finish.
1. Close the Theater tab. In **Billing & Usage**, a green dot under **Recent runs** marks anything that is still active.

A stopped World stays active and keeps using credits until you deactivate it. Deactivating a World does not deactivate the project's Robot Systems: deactivate each file you activated.

## Next: Connect a Robot System

To drive the Jackal of this World, add a Robot System to the same project. Download its two documents first: [jackal.gw](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/get_started/quick_start/files/jackal.gw), the simulation gateway document, and [jackal.sddm](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/get_started/quick_start/files/jackal.sddm), the mobile robot document.

1. In the project, create a Robot System named `jackal` and open it with **Station · Edit** ([Create a File](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/files/#1-create-a-file)). In the **Store**, install `sodero.actuator_gateway`, `sodero.mlc` and `sodero.strider` ([Apps and Packages](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/apps/index.md)).
1. Add a **Gateway** node that runs `sodero.actuator_gateway` and name it `sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal` ([Add a Node](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/graph/#1-add-a-node)). In its inspector, click **Upload** under **Gateway project** and import `jackal.gw` ([Documents and Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/documents/index.md)).
1. Under the gateway document, set **Robot name** to `jackal`, the name of the robot's prim in the World. `jackal.gw` already fills it in ([Name the Robot](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/world_connection/#2-name-the-robot)).
1. Add a **Controller** node that runs `sodero.mlc` and name it `sodero.mlc.jackal`. Click **Upload** under **document (robot)** and import `jackal.sddm`. Connect the node's `servo_link` port to the gateway ([Connect Ports](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/graph/#3-connect-ports)).
1. Add `sodero.strider` and connect its `mobile_base` port to `sodero.mlc.jackal` ([Set Up the Nodes](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/strider/#1-set-up-the-nodes)).
1. Activate and run the World again (Steps 3 and 4). In the Station, click **Go live**, then **Start all nodes** ([Start and Monitor Nodes](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/run/index.md)). Right-click `sodero.strider`, open Strider and drive the Jackal ([Strider](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/strider/index.md)).

For other robots, use documents made for this Station release, such as those in **Sodero Assets** ([Compatibility](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/reference/compatibility/index.md)).
# Account and Workspaces

# Sign In and Account

One Sodero account signs you in to the Sodero Cloud portal at [app.sodero.io](https://app.sodero.io) and to the apps you open from it: Stellar Station, Studio and Theater. This page covers creating the account, signing in, accepting invitations and managing your account.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Create an Account

1. Open [app.sodero.io](https://app.sodero.io) and click **Create an account** under the sign-in form.
1. Enter your **Email** and a **Password** of at least 8 characters, and click **Create account**.
1. On *Check your email*, type the code from Sodero's email and click **Verify** (**Resend code** sends a new one). On *Email verified*, click **Continue**.
1. Answer the five profile questions, one per screen, and click **Get started**. The first question asks for your name, which the people in your workspaces see.

To use your Google account instead, click **Continue with Google** and choose the account. A new account then answers the profile questions.

**Your first workspace.** If you do not belong to a workspace yet, Sodero Cloud creates one for you, named after you, with you as its owner ([Workspaces and People](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/workspaces/index.md)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Sign In

Open [app.sodero.io](https://app.sodero.io), enter your **Email** and **Password** and click **Continue**, or click **Continue with Google**. The portal opens on **Projects**.

The sign-in screen

### Reset a Forgotten Password

1. On the sign-in form, click the forgotten-password link under **Password**.
1. Enter your **Email** and click **Send code**.
1. Enter the **Code from the email** and a **New password** of at least 8 characters, and click **Reset password**. Then sign in with the new password.

### First Sign-In to an Account Sodero Set Up for You

Sign in with your email address and the temporary password from Sodero's email, if you received one. On *Choose a new password*, enter a **New password** (and the **Code from the email**, if asked) and click **Set password**.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Accept an Invitation

People invite you by email. The email has a **Review access** button that opens the portal with the invitation.

| Invitation to         | Email subject                   | In the portal                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A project             | *Sodero project access: NAME*   | **Accept invitation** (steps below)                                                                                                                                                           |
| A Stellar design file | *Sodero access: NAME*           | **Accept invitation** or **Decline**, on a page titled *Invite received*                                                                                                                      |
| A workspace           | *Sodero workspace access: NAME* | Accepted when you open the link while signed in ([Join a Workspace from an Invitation](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/workspaces/#4-join-a-workspace-from-an-invitation)) |

A Stellar design file is a robot or gateway document saved in Stellar Designer ([Make Documents in Stellar Designer](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/documents/#4-make-documents-in-stellar-designer)).

To accept a project invitation:

1. In the email, click **Review access**. *Project invite received* shows the project, the invited address and who invited you.
1. If you are not signed in, click **Sign in**, or **Create an account** if you are new. Use the address the invitation was sent to. After you sign in, the invitation page comes back.
1. Click **Accept invitation**. The portal opens a moment later.

The project appears in **Projects** if you are a member of its workspace; otherwise it is a [guest project](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/workspaces/#guest-projects). A project invitation has no **Decline** button: if you do not want to join, ignore the email. Project invitations expire after 7 days.

| Message                        | What to do                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| *Wrong account*                | You are signed in with another address. Click **Sign out**, then sign in with the invited address. |
| *Invite has expired.*          | Ask for a new invitation.                                                                          |
| *Invite is no longer pending.* | The invitation was already accepted, declined or cancelled.                                        |
| *Invitation not found.*        | The link is incomplete, or the invitation no longer exists. Ask for a new one.                     |

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Account Settings

Click your avatar at the bottom of the left navigation bar and choose **Account Settings**.

The Account settings dialog

| To change           | Do this                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Your name           | Under **Basic info**, click **Edit** next to **Name**, type the name and click **Save**.                                                                                                                         |
| Your photo          | Under **Profile**, click **Change photo**, then **Upload photo** (PNG, JPEG or WebP) or pick a color. **Remove** goes back to a plain color.                                                                     |
| Your email address  | Click **Edit** next to **Email**, type the new address and click **Save**. Then type the code sent to the new address in the **Code** row and click **Confirm**. Until then, your account keeps the old address. |
| Emails about Sodero | Under **Email preferences**, turn **Product updates & news** on or off.                                                                                                                                          |

Your name and photo are shown to the people in your workspaces.

**Connected AI agents** lists the AI agents connected to your account and lets you revoke them ([AI Agents](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/ai_agents/#review-and-revoke-agents)).

To change the theme, click your avatar, choose **Theme**, pick **Midnight** (dark, the default) or **Twilight** (light) and click **Apply**.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Sign-In & Security

Click your avatar and choose **Sign-in & Security**.

Sign-in methods and active sessions

| Setting                            | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Password** › **Update password** | Enter your **Current password** and a **New password** of at least 8 characters, then click **Save**. Shown only for accounts that have a password.                                                    |
| **Google** › **Connect**           | Lets you also sign in with **Continue with Google**                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Google** › **Disconnect**        | Ends sign-in with Google. Works only when your account has another way to sign in.                                                                                                                     |
| **Sign out everywhere**            | Signs your account out on every device, including this one, without asking first. If you lose a device or think that someone knows your password, use it, then sign in again and update your password. |

To sign out of this browser only, click your avatar, choose **Sign out** and confirm. This also signs you out of the apps you opened from the portal.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Delete Your Account

**Deleting your account cannot be undone.** It also deletes every workspace you own, with all its projects, and every project you created in other people's workspaces, for everyone who works in them.

Deleting your account also removes your profile, your Stellar design files, your memberships, and the Robot Systems and Robot Worlds you created in other people's projects. A workspace you own is deleted with every project in it, including projects that other members created.

Before you delete your account:

1. [Transfer ownership](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/workspaces/#7-transfer-ownership) of every workspace that other people still use.
1. [Download local copies](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/projects/#6-download-a-local-copy) of the Robot Systems and Robot Worlds that you or others want to keep.
1. Deactivate whatever is still active in your workspaces and projects.

Then open **Account Settings**, click **Delete account** and confirm with **Delete**. The portal signs you out. If a message asks you to contact support, part of the deletion did not finish: contact Sodero.

______________________________________________________________________

## Sign-In Messages

| Message                                                     | What to do                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| *Email or password is incorrect.*                           | Check both. If you forgot the password, [reset it](#reset-a-forgotten-password).   |
| *Please confirm your email before signing in.*              | Enter the code from the verification email.                                        |
| *That code is not correct. …* or *That code has expired. …* | Use the code from the most recent email, or ask for a new code.                    |
| *No account uses this email address.*                       | Check the address, or create an account.                                           |
| *Reset your password to sign in.*                           | [Reset your password](#reset-a-forgotten-password), then sign in with the new one. |
| *This account needs an administrator to finish its setup.*  | Contact Sodero.                                                                    |
| *Sign-in didn't finish*                                     | Google sign-in was cancelled or refused. Click **Back to sign in** and try again.  |

# Workspaces and People

A workspace is where a team works together in the Sodero Cloud portal. It holds the team's projects and people, the project libraries, and one plan with its credits ([Billing and Usage](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/billing/index.md)).

______________________________________________________________________

## The Workspace Menu

You can belong to several workspaces. The portal shows one at a time: its name is at the top left of the page, followed by a badge with your role. Click the name to open the workspace menu.

The workspace menu of Acme Robotics

The menu holds **Switch workspace**, **Create workspace**, **Workspace settings** (owner only), **People**, **Billing & Usage** ([Billing and Usage](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/billing/index.md)) and **Leave workspace**. Everyone in the workspace can open **People** and **Billing & Usage**.

______________________________________________________________________

## Roles

Everyone in a workspace has one role: **Owner**, **Admin** or **Member**. A workspace has exactly one owner. Roles inside a project are separate: see [Project Access and Roles](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/projects/#4-project-access-and-roles).

| Action                                                                                                | Owner | Admin          | Member                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Invite people                                                                                         | Yes   | As Member only | No                                                        |
| Remove people                                                                                         | Yes   | Members only   | No                                                        |
| Change roles, cancel invitations, change workspace settings, transfer ownership, delete the workspace | Yes   | No             | No                                                        |
| Create projects                                                                                       | Yes   | Yes            | When **Members can create projects** is on                |
| Add, export and delete files in project libraries                                                     | Yes   | Yes            | When **Members can manage the Library** is on             |
| Manage every project in the workspace, **Empty all trash**                                            | Yes   | Yes            | No: members have the role they were given in each project |

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Create a Workspace

Open the workspace menu, choose **Create workspace**, enter a name of up to 30 characters and click **Create**. You are the owner of the new workspace, and the portal switches to it. Each workspace has its own plan and credits.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Switch Between Workspaces

Open the workspace menu, point at **Switch workspace** and click a workspace. A check mark shows the current one.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Invite People

Owners and admins invite people by email.

1. Open the workspace menu and choose **People**.
1. Under **Invite by email**, type the person's email address.
1. Choose the role: **Member** (the default) or **Admin**. Only the owner can invite admins.
1. Click **Invite**. The invitation is sent at once, without **Save**.

The People dialog

The person receives an email titled *Sodero workspace access: NAME* with a **Review access** button. An invitation is valid for 7 days; inviting the same address again replaces it. The owner sees open invitations in the list, marked **Pending**. If the dialog says *Couldn't send invitation. Try again.*, check the address; people who are already members cannot be invited.

**Tip:** To share one project only, invite the person to that project instead ([Share and Collaborate](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/sharing/index.md)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Join a Workspace from an Invitation

1. Sign in with the address the invitation was sent to. If you do not have an account yet, [create one](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/sign_in/#1-create-an-account) with that address first.
1. While you are signed in, open the invitation email and click **Review access**. The portal accepts the invitation at once.
1. Open the workspace menu, point at **Switch workspace** and choose the new workspace.

If the portal says *Invite has expired.*, ask for a new invitation. If it says *You're signed in with a different account. …*, sign out, sign in with the address the invitation was sent to and open the link again.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Manage Members and Invitations

Open the workspace menu and choose **People**. Under **Members & roles**, each person has a row with their name, email address and role.

- **Change a role** (owner): choose **Admin** or **Member** in the person's role menu.
- **Remove a person**: click **×** on their row. The owner can remove admins and members; admins can remove members.
- **Cancel an invitation** (owner): click **×** on the row of the pending invitation.

Click **Save** to apply the changes; **Cancel** discards them. Nobody can change their own role or remove themselves. Members see the list read-only.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Change Workspace Settings

Only the owner sees **Workspace settings** in the workspace menu.

| Section         | What you can do                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Profile**     | **Change color** sets the color behind the workspace's initial; **Remove** resets it.                                                                 |
| **Basic info**  | Edit **Name** (up to 30 characters) and click **Save**                                                                                                |
| **Permissions** | **Members can create projects**, and **Members can manage the Library** (add, export and delete files in project libraries). Both are off by default. |

The color and the permissions are saved as soon as you change them. The dialog also holds [Transfer ownership](#7-transfer-ownership) and [Delete workspace](#8-delete-a-workspace).

______________________________________________________________________

## 7. Transfer Ownership

1. In **Workspace settings**, under **Ownership**, click **Transfer ownership**. The button stays disabled until someone else has joined the workspace.
1. Choose the new owner from the members and click **Next**.
1. Click **Transfer ownership** to confirm, then **Done**.

You become an admin.

______________________________________________________________________

## 8. Delete a Workspace

**Deleting a workspace cannot be undone.** It permanently deletes every project, file and setting in the workspace, and everyone loses access.

Before you delete a workspace, deactivate its active Robot Systems and Robot Worlds and [download local copies](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/projects/#6-download-a-local-copy) of anything you want to keep.

1. In **Workspace settings**, under **Delete workspace**, click **Delete workspace**.
1. Type the workspace's exact name and click **Delete**. The portal opens your next workspace.

______________________________________________________________________

## 9. Leave a Workspace

Open the workspace menu, choose **Leave workspace** and click **Leave**. You lose access to the workspace and its projects, except projects you were invited to directly. To come back, someone must invite you again.

The owner cannot leave (*You're the only owner of this workspace. Transfer ownership before leaving.*): [transfer ownership](#7-transfer-ownership) first.

______________________________________________________________________

## Guest Projects

A guest project is a project you were invited to without being a member of its workspace. To see your guest projects, open the workspace menu, point at **Switch workspace** and choose **Guest projects (N)**, shown when you have some.

In this view, the top bar reads **Guest workspace**, and **Trash** and **Notifications** are hidden. In each project, you have the role you were invited with. Guest projects use the credits of the workspace they belong to.

______________________________________________________________________

The left navigation bar, **Notifications** and the **Help** menu are described in [Find Your Way in the Portal](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/get_started/sodero_cloud/#find-your-way-in-the-portal).

# Billing and Usage

Robot Systems and Robot Worlds use credits while they are active. Credits belong to a workspace. This page explains what uses credits, how to read **Billing & Usage**, and what happens when credits run out.

______________________________________________________________________

## How Credits Work

- **Credits belong to a workspace.** Everything active in the workspace's projects uses its balance, whoever activated it, guests and AI agents included.
- **Each workspace has one plan.** Your workspace's plan sets how many credits the workspace receives, how many credits per hour each kind of use takes, and the workspace's limits. **Billing & Usage** shows them.
- **Credits renew every week or every month**, depending on the plan, on the workspace's own cycle. Unused plan credits expire at renewal; they do not roll over.
- **Extra credits from Sodero** can have their own end date. The credits that expire soonest are used first.

______________________________________________________________________

## What Uses Credits

| What                                        | Uses credits                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| An active Robot System or Robot World       | By the hour from **Activate** to **Deactivate**, whether or not anything runs in it and whether or not anyone uses it |
| Each Theater viewer and each Studio session | While it is open, at your plan's rate for its rendering mode, **RTX Real-time** or **WebGPU**                         |
| The robot cameras of an active World        | While the cameras are rendered                                                                                        |

**Billing & Usage** shows how many credits each of these uses on your workspace's plan.

**Stop is not Deactivate.** A stopped Robot System or Robot World is still active and still uses credits. Only **Deactivate**, or [Auto off](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#5-auto-off), ends the use ([Activate and Run](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/get_started/key_concepts/#activate-and-run)).

Storage, AI agent tool calls and the Project VPN do not use credits; they count against your plan's [limits](#limits).

______________________________________________________________________

## The Billing & Usage Dialog

Open the workspace menu and choose **Billing & Usage**. Everyone in the workspace can open it. It shows the current workspace and updates while it is open. It calls a Robot System a *System*, a Robot World a *World*, and the time one of them is active a *run*.

The top line shows your workspace's plan and, next to **Renews**, the date of the next renewal. A red **Out of credits** badge appears when the balance is zero.

### Credits

| Row                                       | Meaning                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **credits left**                          | The workspace's balance: the plan credits and extra credits that are left                                |
| **Weekly credits** or **Monthly credits** | The credits the plan gives the workspace at each renewal                                                 |
| **Used this week** or **Used this month** | Credits used since the last renewal                                                                      |
| **Used in total**                         | Credits used since the workspace was created                                                             |
| **Extra credits from Sodero**             | The extra credits left, each with its end date. Shown only when there are some.                          |
| **Used beyond the balance**               | Credits used after the balance reached zero, on plans that keep running. Shown only when there are some. |

Under the rows, a line gives your plan's rates: the credits per hour of a System, of a World and of each kind of renderer.

### Limits

Each meter compares what the workspace uses with what the plan allows. The bar turns yellow at 80 % and red when the limit is reached. At the limit, the action that would go over it is refused with a [message](#messages).

| Meter                                  | What it counts                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Projects**                           | The workspace's projects. Projects in Trash do not count.                                  |
| **Workspace storage**                  | Everything stored in the workspace's projects: files, saved versions and project libraries |
| **Project libraries**                  | The files in the libraries of the workspace's projects                                     |
| **Systems and Worlds running at once** | The Robot Systems and Robot Worlds active right now in the workspace                       |

### AI Agents and Project VPN This Month

**AI agent (MCP) tool calls**, **Project VPN time** and **Project VPN data** count the workspace's use of [AI agents](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/ai_agents/index.md) and of the [Project VPN](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/project_vpn/index.md). They count per calendar month (UTC); the line under them gives the reset date. When the plan also limits tool calls per minute, the line says so: *Agents can make up to N tool calls per minute.* When a counter reaches its limit, agent tool calls are refused, or Project VPN connections end, until the reset.

### Recent Runs

The table lists the workspace's recent runs, with the columns **Run**, **Started**, **Time** and **Credits**. Under each name, the row shows its kind and its project:

| Kind                                            | What it is                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| *System*, *World*                               | A Robot System or Robot World, from Activate to Deactivate |
| *World viewer (RTX)*, *World viewer (WebGPU)*   | A Theater viewer                                           |
| *World camera renderer*                         | The robot cameras of an active World                       |
| *Cosmic Editor (RTX)*, *Cosmic Editor (WebGPU)* | A Studio session                                           |

A row with a green dot is still active and still using credits; its time counts up.

______________________________________________________________________

## When Credits Run Out

What happens at zero depends on your plan. On plans that stop at zero, the rates line ends with *When credits run out, runs stop and new runs can't start.*

| Plan          | At zero credits                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Stops at zero | The **Out of credits** badge appears. The workspace's active Robot Systems and Robot Worlds are deactivated, and activating one fails with *This workspace has run out of credits. …* |
| Keeps running | Work goes on. Credits used beyond zero show as **Used beyond the balance** and are taken from the next credits the workspace receives.                                                |

New plan credits arrive at the next renewal. There is no payment page in the portal: to change your workspace's plan or to add credits, contact Sodero.

______________________________________________________________________

## Save Credits

- **Deactivate when you are done.** A stopped Robot System or Robot World is still active and still uses credits.
- **Keep Auto off on.** A Robot System or Robot World that someone forgot then deactivates by itself.
- **Close the views you no longer need.** Theater viewers and Studio sessions can use credits while they are open; the rates line shows what each rendering mode uses.
- **Check Recent runs.** Rows with a green dot are still using credits.

______________________________________________________________________

## Messages

| Message                                                                            | What to do                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| *This workspace has run out of credits. …*                                         | Wait for the next renewal, or contact Sodero to add credits.                                                     |
| *The PLAN plan runs at most N Systems and Worlds at once. …*                       | Deactivate a Robot System or Robot World, then activate the new one. Stopping it is not enough.                  |
| *The PLAN plan holds up to N projects in a workspace. …*                           | Move a project you no longer need to Trash, or contact Sodero. Also shown when you restore a project from Trash. |
| *Not enough workspace storage: …* or *Not enough room in the project libraries: …* | The upload does not fit. Delete files you no longer need, or contact Sodero.                                     |
| *This workspace's plan doesn't include …*                                          | The plan has no AI agent tool calls or no Project VPN. Contact Sodero.                                           |
| *Limit reached: … for this month. It renews on DATE.*                              | The monthly allowance is used up until the date shown.                                                           |
# Projects and Files

# Projects

A project holds the Robot Systems and Robot Worlds that belong together and decides who can open them. Every project belongs to a workspace.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. The Project List

Click **Projects** in the left navigation bar. The portal also opens here after you sign in.

The project list of Acme Robotics

Each row shows the project's name and description, its **Contents** (for example *1 System · 1 World*), its **Members**, **My access** (your [role](#4-project-access-and-roles)) and **Last modified**. A star marks a favorite, and a green **Running** badge shows while a file of the project is active.

Click a project to open it. The **⋯** button at the end of a row opens the project menu:

| Item                  | Shown to | Does                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Manage access**     | Managers | Invites people, changes roles and sets the project access ([Share and Collaborate](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/sharing/index.md)) |
| **Add to favorites**  | Everyone | Lists the project under **Favorites** on **Home**                                                                                                         |
| **Duplicate project** | Managers | [Copies the project](#duplicate-a-project)                                                                                                                |
| **Project settings**  | Managers | [Name, description and project information](#rename-or-describe-a-project)                                                                                |
| **Move to trash**     | Managers | [Moves the project to Trash](#7-move-to-trash-restore-and-delete)                                                                                         |

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Create a Project

1. On the project list, click **+ Project**. A workspace without projects also offers **Create new project**.
1. Enter a **Name** (up to 20 characters) and, if you like, a **Description** (up to 40 characters).
1. Choose the **Project access**: **Restricted** (*Invited people only*, the default) or **Workspace** (*All members of this workspace*).
1. Click **Create**. The new project opens.

The Create project dialog

- If **+ Project** is dimmed, only the workspace's owner and admins can create projects there. The owner can turn on **Members can create projects** ([Workspaces and People](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/workspaces/#6-change-workspace-settings)).
- Your workspace's plan limits how many projects the workspace can hold; projects in Trash do not count ([Billing and Usage](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/billing/#limits)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. The Project Page

Click a project on the list to open it. The top bar shows **Projects** (back to the list), the project's name and your access.

Warehouse Demo, with the Robot System jackal and the Robot World warehouse

| Control                       | Does                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Project VPN**               | Connects your computer to the project's Stations ([Project VPN](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/project_vpn/index.md))              |
| **AI agents**                 | Shows how to connect an AI agent, and the project link to give it ([AI Agents](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/ai_agents/index.md)) |
| **Search files**, **Filters** | Show only the files whose name contains a text, or of one type or state                                                                                |
| **Import**                    | Creates a file from an `.sdr` file ([Import an .sdr File](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/files/#2-import-an-sdr-file))            |
| **New file**                  | Creates a Robot System or a Robot World ([Create a File](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/files/#1-create-a-file))                  |

Editors and managers also see the selection bar under the toolbar (*0 selected · Worlds: 0/1*, **Clear**, **Actions**), which handles [several files at once](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#4-several-files-at-once).

The files are listed in two tables, **Robot Systems** and **Robot Worlds**. Each row shows the file's **Activation** and **Running** state, the **Actions** links that open it, a Station's **IP address**, **Auto off**, **Active users**, **Resource** use and **Last modified** ([Activate and Run](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/index.md)). Clicking a row selects the file; files open only from their **Actions** links. The **⋯** button at the end of a row holds the [file actions](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/files/#3-file-actions).

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Project Access and Roles

**Project access** decides who can open the project: only the people invited to it (**Restricted**, the default), or also every member of the workspace (**Workspace**). Managers change it in **Manage access** ([Share and Collaborate](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/sharing/#1-invite-people)).

Each person in a project has one of three roles, shown in lists as Manager, Editor and Viewer:

- **Can manage**, for people who look after the project: access, copies, downloads and Trash.
- **Can edit**, for people who build and run the Robot Systems and Robot Worlds.
- **Can view**, for people who look and review without changing anything.

The person who created a project can manage it, and so can the workspace's owner and admins.

| Action                                                                       | Can view  | Can edit | Can manage |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | -------- | ---------- |
| Open the project; see its files, their **Activation** state and active users | ✓         | ✓        | ✓          |
| See the **Running** state of an active file                                  | —         | ✓        | ✓          |
| Open **Station · Edit**, **Station · Live**, **Studio** and **Theater**      | view only | ✓        | ✓          |
| Create, import, duplicate, rename and trash files                            | —         | ✓        | ✓          |
| Activate, run, stop and deactivate files; change **Auto off**                | —         | ✓        | ✓          |
| Download a local copy of a file                                              | —         | —        | ✓          |
| Invite people, change roles, set the project access                          | —         | —        | ✓          |
| Duplicate the project, change its settings, move it to Trash                 | —         | —        | ✓          |
| Restore or permanently delete the project's items in Trash                   | —         | —        | ✓          |

Controls you cannot use are dimmed and give the reason on hover. Creating projects, managing project libraries and **Empty all trash** depend on your [workspace role](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/workspaces/#roles).

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Rename and Duplicate a Project

### Rename or Describe a Project

Open the project's **⋯** menu, choose **Project settings**, change **Project Name** (up to 20 characters) or **Description**, and click **Save**.

### Duplicate a Project

Choose **⋯ › Duplicate project**. The copy, for example *Warehouse Demo copy*, is created in the same workspace, with the same description and project access.

- Every Robot System and Robot World is copied with its files. Each Station copy keeps its documents and its apps.
- Official Sodero Worlds, and the official Sodero files that other Worlds use, are left out. A message names them.
- Check **Manage access** on the copy and invite the people who need it.
- The copy counts toward your plan's project limit.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Download a Local Copy

Managers can keep a Robot System or Robot World outside Sodero: open the file's **⋯** menu on the project page and choose **Download local copy**. The browser saves an `.sdr` file named after the file, for example `jackal.sdr`. To keep a whole project, download each of its files.

Use the copy to keep a backup, to [import it](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/files/#2-import-an-sdr-file) into another project, or to move a Robot System to Stellar X ([Move Robot Systems Between Stellar X and Sodero Cloud](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/files/#move-robot-systems-between-stellar-x-and-sodero-cloud)).

**Tip:** A Station saves its data when it deactivates. Deactivate the Robot System before you download it, so that the copy holds your latest changes.

Official Sodero content stays in Sodero. An official Sodero World cannot be downloaded, and a World that uses official Sodero files is downloaded without them.

______________________________________________________________________

## 7. Move to Trash, Restore and Delete

To move a project to Trash, open its **⋯** menu on the project list, choose **Move to trash** and confirm. Its active files are deactivated first, which ends their use of credits.

Click **Trash** in the left navigation bar to see the trashed projects, Robot Systems and Robot Worlds. The **⋯** menu of an entry, shown to the people who can manage it, offers:

- **Restore**, which puts it back. Restoring a project needs room under your plan's project limit.
- **Delete permanently**, which removes it for good. This cannot be undone.

Workspace owners and admins also have **Empty all trash**: after asking, it permanently deletes every entry they can manage.

**Library files do not go to Trash.** Deleting a file from a project's library removes it at once ([Libraries](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/libraries/index.md)).

# Robot Systems and Robot Worlds

A project holds two kinds of file: **Robot Systems**, which run robot software in Stellar Station, and **Robot Worlds**, which simulate the place where the robots work.

| File             | What it is                                                                        | Edit it in         | Work with it live in |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | -------------------- |
| **Robot System** | One Stellar Station ("the Station"): its node graph, documents, settings and apps | **Station · Edit** | **Station · Live**   |
| **Robot World**  | A simulated environment: a scene with your robots, the ground and lighting        | **Studio**         | **Theater**          |
