| Title            | The node name                                                                                                                                          |
| Second line      | The app or module the node runs                                                                                                                        |
| **REQUIRES n/m** | Ports the node needs from other nodes, on the left edge of the card: connected / total                                                                 |
| **PROVIDES n/m** | Ports the node offers, on the right edge: ports with at least one connection / total                                                                   |
| State            | **Planned** until the node first starts, then its running state ([Node States](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/run/#4-node-states)) |

The card border has the color of the node type: orange for gateways, blue-violet for controllers, purple for compounds and mint for applications. The arrow at the top right of a card folds its ports away.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Connect Ports

Connect a port that one node requires to a matching port that another node provides:

- **Drag** from one port dot to the other.
- **Click** one port, then the other.
- In the inspector of the node that requires the port, click **Auto-connect** next to the port. The Station connects the first matching port it finds, or shows *No match*.

The Station accepts a connection only when the two ports are on different nodes, one requires and the other provides, and both use the same interface. The inspector shows each port's interface under its name, for example `api.actuator.servo.v1`. The Station also keeps the system's structure:

- Only a controller may use a gateway.
- An application uses controllers or compounds, never gateways directly.
- One controller drives a gateway.

A refused connection says why, for example *Connect ports on different nodes with opposite directions and matching contracts.*

To remove a connection, select the node and click **Disconnect** next to the port in the inspector.

**Check Auto-connect with several robots.** Auto-connect does not look at node names: with two gateways in the graph, it may pick the other robot's. Check the result, or drag the connection yourself.

### Common Connections

| Node (requires)                                               | Port                | Connect to (provides)                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sodero.mmc.<name>`, `sodero.mlc.<name>`, `sodero.amc.<name>` | `servo_link`        | The robot's actuator gateway `sodero.actuator_gateway.<name>`, port `servo_link` |
| `sodero.strider`                                              | `mobile_base`       | The mobile base controller `sodero.mlc.<name>`, port `mobile_base`               |
| `sodero.strider`                                              | `localization`      | The localizer `sodero.icp_localizer`, port `localization`                        |
| `sodero.strider`                                              | `navigation`        | The navigator `sodero.navigator`, port `navigation`                              |
| `sodero.icp_localizer`                                        | `camera` (required) | The robot's camera gateway `sodero.camera_gateway.<name>`, port `camera`         |
| `sodero.navigator`                                            | `mobile_base`       | The mobile base controller `sodero.mlc.<name>`, port `mobile_base`               |
| `sodero.navigator`                                            | `localization`      | The localizer `sodero.icp_localizer`, port `localization`                        |

Strider drives what its ports are connected to ([Strider](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/strider/index.md)).

**For navigation**, install `sodero.icp_localizer` and `sodero.navigator` from the Store ([Apps and Packages](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/apps/index.md)) and add them. The localizer needs its `camera` port connected; the navigator drives the base connected to its `mobile_base` port and follows the robot's position from the localizer connected to its `localization` port. Both read the Station's map bundle ([Documents and Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/documents/#2-kinds-of-documents)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Rename and Delete

- **Rename:** click the pencil next to the node name in the inspector and enter the new name. The node keeps its connections and the documents it uses.
- **Delete:** right-click the node and choose **Delete node**. The dialog asks *Delete "…" from this robot system?*; click **Delete node**. The node's connections are removed too.

On the Live page, stop a node before you rename or delete it.

Deleting a node cannot be undone. Everyone working on the Station sees the change at once.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Find Your Way in a Large Graph

- **Filter** shows only nodes of one **Node type** or **Status**; **Reset all** clears it.
- **Fit view** zooms to show every node; **Auto layout** arranges the nodes by their connections.
- The **N issues** chip at the left of the toolbar lists problems, such as *Required port "servo_link" is not connected*. **Locate** jumps to the node.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Load and Export the Graph

- **Export** downloads the graph as a `.yaml` file. If something runs on the Live page that the graph does not show, it asks first: **Planned topology only** or **Also include what is running**.
- **Load YAML** loads such a file from your PC (**From your PC**) or from the project library (**Project Library**). It replaces the nodes and connections of the Station (*… loaded — N nodes now in the system.*).

The file holds the graph only: nodes, their parameters and their connections. Documents, settings and apps are not part of it. To copy a whole Robot System, use **Duplicate file**, or **Download local copy** and **Import**, on the project page ([Robot Systems and Robot Worlds](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/files/index.md)).

# Documents and Settings

Most nodes work from a **document**: a gateway runs a gateway document (`.gw`), a robot controller runs a robot document (`.sdd`, `.sddm` or `.sdda`). Some apps also have **settings** that you edit in the node's inspector. This page shows how to give a node its document, which kinds exist, and how to change settings. You can do all of this on the Edit page and on the Live page, while the node is stopped.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Choose or Upload a Document

Select the node. The **Parameters** section of its inspector has one field for each document the app reads, for example **Gateway project** on an actuator gateway or **document (robot)** on a controller.

The inspector of an actuator gateway, with its gateway document jackal and the Robot name under Parameters

- **A new node starts from a blank document.** When you add an actuator gateway or a robot controller, the Station gives it a document named after the node that holds a blank template: for `sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal`, the document `jackal` with the file `default.gw`. A robot controller's template is `default.sdd`, `default.sddm` or `default.sdda`. Upload the document made for your robot in its place.
- The dropdown lists the documents of that kind in the Station. A field that a controller requires reads *Select a required document* until it names one; other fields may offer **Built-in default (no document)**. Built-in defaults do not describe your robot: give every gateway and controller the document made for it.
- The line under the field tells which file the document holds, for example *Uploaded: jackal.gw · 1.2 KB · …*, or *Not uploaded*.

| Button     | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Upload** | Brings in a new document ([Upload a Document](#upload-a-document))                                                                                                                                         |
| **Edit**   | Opens the document in its editor in a new tab: the Gateway Designer for a gateway document, Stellar Designer for a robot document                                                                          |
| **Delete** | Next to an uploaded file: puts the document back to its blank template. The Station asks first, for example *Delete jackal.gw? The gateway-project document jackal becomes the blank template default.gw.* |

### Upload a Document

1. Click **Upload** under the field. The dialog is named after the kind, for example **Upload gateway-project document** or **Upload robot document**.

1. Choose where the file comes from:

   | Tab                   | Files                                                                                                                                    |
   | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   | **From your PC**      | Drop the file on the dialog, or click **Choose file**                                                                                    |
   | **Workspace Library** | The files of the project library ([Libraries](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/libraries/index.md))                   |
   | **Sodero Assets**     | Robot and gateway documents published by Sodero, under **Manipulator**, **Mobile** and **Legged**. Only for robot and gateway documents. |

1. Click **Import**.

Uploading a gateway document from your PC

The same dialog for a robot document

The Station confirms the upload, for example *jackal.gw uploaded as the gateway-project document jackal*, and the node takes the new document. If the upload fails, the message says why: *… was not uploaded — …*.

- If the field already names a document, the upload replaces that document.
- A new document is named after the last part of the node name: for `sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal` it is `jackal` ([Name the Node](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/graph/#name-the-node)).

### Rules

- **A running node is locked.** While a node runs, its inspector says *This node is running. Stop it to change its documents, parameters, settings, ports or name.* Stop the node before you upload, edit or delete its document or change its settings.
- **Each controller takes its own kind:** `.sdd` for `sodero.mmc`, `.sddm` for `sodero.mlc`, `.sdda` for `sodero.amc`.
- **A robot document names its gateway** and the gateway's actuators it uses. Connect the controller's `servo_link` to that gateway, and give the gateway at least as many actuators as the document uses.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Kinds of Documents

| Kind                 | File                                                                                      | Used by                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Gateway document     | `.gw`                                                                                     | Actuator gateways, `sodero.actuator_gateway.<name>`                                                                                                                                                            |
| Robot document       | `.sdd` (manipulator), `.sddm` (mobile base), `.sdda` (articulated robot)                  | `sodero.mmc.<name>`, `sodero.mlc.<name>`, `sodero.amc.<name>`                                                                                                                                                  |
| Tool bank, Pose bank | `.tool`, `.pose`, exported from Motion Studio                                             | The manipulator controller `sodero.mmc.<name>`, in its **Tool bank** and **Pose bank** fields. [Motion Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/motion_studio/index.md) edits them in place. |
| Camera document      | `.yaml`                                                                                   | Camera gateways, `sodero.camera_gateway.<name>`                                                                                                                                                                |
| IMU document         | `imu.yaml`, created in the node's settings                                                | IMU gateways, `sodero.imu_gateway.<name>`                                                                                                                                                                      |
| GNSS document        | A gateway document that holds `gnss.yaml`, created in the node's settings                 | GNSS gateways, `sodero.gnss_gateway.<name>`                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Map bundle           | A `.nav` folder packed as `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`, `.tar` or `.zip`, for example `site.nav.tgz` | The localizer, the navigator and visual odometry                                                                                                                                                               |

A Station has **one map bundle**: the localizer, the navigator and visual odometry share it, and a new upload replaces it. What a map bundle holds is described in [Load and Configure a Map](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/latest/navigation/map_bundle/) in the Stellar X manual.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Settings

Some apps declare settings. The inspector then shows one section per settings file below **Parameters**, titled by the app.

1. Stop the node if it runs.
1. Change the fields.
1. Click **Save settings** (*Settings saved.*). **Discard and reload** discards your changes.
1. When the settings belong to a document, the section shows once the node has one: *Choose or upload a … document in Parameters; its … settings then appear here.*
1. Some apps can create the file for you: click **Create with defaults**. An IMU or GNSS gateway without a document creates one here: enter a name under **New … document** and click **Create**.
1. The fields themselves come from each app.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Make Documents in Stellar Designer

Gateway and robot documents are made in **Stellar Designer**: the Gateway Designer makes `.gw` documents, and the manipulator, mobile robot and articulation editors make `.sdd`, `.sddm` and `.sdda` documents. **Edit** in the inspector opens a node's document there. Every editor and field is described in the Stellar X manual: [Stellar Designer](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/latest/tutorials/stellar_designer/introduction/) and [Gateway Designer](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/latest/gateways/gateway_designer/).

- The robot that a simulation gateway drives in the World is set on the gateway node, as its **Robot name** ([Connect to the World](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/world_connection/#2-name-the-robot)).
- Ready-made documents for Sodero's robots are in **Sodero Assets**.

### Documents in an Obsolete Format

Documents from an older Stellar Designer use an obsolete format, and the Station refuses them: the message says that the file *uses an obsolete format*, or names an *Obsolete robot file* or an *Obsolete gateway filename*. A robot document without `runtime.yaml`, the file that names its controller, is refused the same way: *The robot document has no runtime.yaml naming its controller.* Export the document again from the current Stellar Designer and upload the new file.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Troubleshooting

| Message                                                                                                                       | What to do                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| *Only … files can be imported.*                                                                                               | The file has the wrong extension for this field. Check the kind in the dialog's title.                                           |
| *… is not a robot document (expected a .sdd, .sddm or .sdda file).*                                                           | Export the robot from Stellar Designer as `.sdd` (manipulator), `.sddm` (mobile) or `.sdda` (articulation)                       |
| *… was not uploaded — This package accepts … documents.*                                                                      | The controller takes another kind of robot document: `.sdd` for `sodero.mmc`, `.sddm` for `sodero.mlc`, `.sdda` for `sodero.amc` |
| *… uses an obsolete format. …*, *Obsolete robot file: …* or *The robot document has no runtime.yaml naming its controller. …* | Export the document again from the current Stellar Designer ([Documents in an Obsolete Format](#documents-with-old-node-names))  |
| *Stop this node before changing its settings: …*                                                                              | Stop the node, then save the settings again                                                                                      |
| *… is an archive but not a .nav bundle (no localizer.yaml inside).* or *…: the .nav bundle is incomplete — missing …*         | Pack the localizer's `.nav` folder itself as `.tar.gz` or `.zip`, and upload that                                                |
| *… is yaml but not a camera_gateway config …*                                                                                 | The file is not a camera document                                                                                                |
| *Another editor changed this robot file first — reload …*                                                                     | Someone else changed the document at the same time. Reload, then repeat your change.                                             |

# Connect to the World

The Robot Systems of a project drive the robots in the project's active Robot World. Sodero Cloud makes the connection: a simulation gateway reaches the World by itself and finds its robot by name. This page shows what to set so that a robot moves.

```
flowchart LR
    subgraph RS ["Robot System"]
        C["Controller<br>sodero.mlc.jackal"] -- servo_link --> G["Simulation gateway<br>sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal<br>Robot name: jackal"]
    end
    subgraph W ["Robot World, active"]
        R["Robot prim jackal<br>joints 1 to 4"]
    end
    G -- "found by name" --> R
```

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. What Is Automatic

- **No address to set.** The simulation, camera and IMU gateways of an active Station reach the project's active World through the local simulator address, which is the default in their documents: Sodero Cloud forwards it to the World. Keep that default; a document that points to another address does not reach the World.
- **Activate in any order.** A Station that is active before the World connects once the World is up.
- **One World per project.** Only one Robot World of a project can be active at a time, and a Station never reaches a World in another project ([How Robot Worlds and Robot Systems Work Together](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/files/#4-how-robot-worlds-and-robot-systems-work-together)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Name the Robot

A simulation gateway drives the robot whose articulation prim has its robot name. You set the robot name on the gateway node in the Station, so that one gateway document fits any robot:

1. Select the simulation gateway node, for example `sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal`.
1. Under **Parameters**, check that **Gateway project** names its gateway document ([Documents and Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/documents/index.md)).
1. In **Robot name**, under the document, enter the name of the robot's articulation prim, for example `jackal` for `/World/jackal`. Press `Enter`, or leave the field, to save it.

A new name applies at the gateway's next start. Without a name, the inspector says *No robot name yet: the gateway is tied to no robot in the World.* Renaming the node does not change the robot it drives.

**The robot name must be exactly the name of the robot's articulation prim in the World.**

| Station                                                                        | World                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Gateway node `sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal` with the **Robot name** `jackal` | The robot's articulation prim `jackal`, at `/World/jackal` in the World's hierarchy |

- Names are case-sensitive: `Jackal` and `jackal` are different robots.
- A robot name uses letters, digits and `_`, and does not start with a digit.
- Every robot in the World needs a name of its own.

If the names differ, the gateway never finds its robot: it keeps waiting, and the robot does not move.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Match Actuators and Joints

The gateway addresses joints by actuator index. Actuator *i* drives the robot's *i*-th movable joint, revolute or prismatic, in the order of the robot's USD file; joints marked `rc:passive = true` are skipped ([Prepare a World for Simulation](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/prepare_world/#3-joints-are-actuators-in-usd-order)).

| Gateway                               | Robot in the World                                           |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Actuators 1, 2, 3, 4 (indices 0 to 3) | The robot's 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th movable joint in USD order |

- Give the gateway one actuator per joint it drives. The robot document then maps the gateway's actuators to its joints or wheels ([Documents and Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/documents/index.md)).
- The **Joints** list in Studio is alphabetical; it does not show this order.
- To drive one robot with two gateways, for example an arm and its gripper, set the gripper gateway's **DOF offset** to the index of the gripper's first joint ([Gateway Designer › Simulation Gateways](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/latest/gateways/gateway_designer/#5-simulation-gateways) in the Stellar X manual).

What a robot needs in the World, such as its articulation and joint drives, is described in [Prepare a World for Simulation](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/prepare_world/index.md).

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Several Robots and Stations

- Use one gateway and one controller per robot, each gateway with its own robot name.
- The gateways can sit in one Robot System or in several. Every active Robot System of the project connects to the same World.
- Drive each robot, or each part of a robot, from one gateway only.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Cameras and IMUs

- **Camera gateway** (`sodero.camera_gateway.<name>`): its camera name must be the name of the camera's prim in the World. It uses letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`. The World renders the robots' cameras while it is active; the first pictures can take a moment after the World starts.
- **IMU gateway** (`sodero.imu_gateway.<name>`): it reads the IMU of one robot, which you name like the robot of an actuator gateway.

The World must declare its cameras and IMUs ([Prepare a World for Simulation](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/prepare_world/index.md)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Start Order

Activate the World and the Robot System and run the World ([Activate and Run](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#how-it-works)), start the gateway before its controller ([Start and Monitor Nodes](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/run/index.md)), then switch the servo on in the controller's UI ([Strider](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/strider/index.md), [Motion Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/motion_studio/index.md), [Articulation](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/articulation/index.md)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 7. Troubleshooting

A gateway connects to the World, not to another node. A World that is not running, or a robot name that does not match, therefore shows neither as **Waiting binding** nor as an error in the graph: the gateway's node can look normal while the gateway waits for its robot. Select the gateway and read its **Gateway events** log ([Logs and Activity](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/run/#5-logs-and-activity)). It says whether the gateway is still waiting for its robot or is connected to the simulation.

| Symptom                                                        | What to check                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The gateway keeps waiting for its robot                        | The World is active and playing; it is in the same project; the gateway's **Robot name** equals the robot's prim name exactly; the gateway document keeps the default simulator address             |
| The controller stays in **Waiting binding**                    | Its `servo_link` is connected to the gateway, and the gateway runs ([Node States](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/run/#4-node-states))                                           |
| The servo switches on, but the robot does not move             | The gateway has as many actuators as the robot document uses. In Strider, the drive mode is **Twist**.                                                                                              |
| A wheel or joint turns the wrong way, or the wrong joint moves | Stop motion. Check the robot's joint order in USD, the actuator mapping of the robot document, the axis direction and the configured polarity. Change the document, then check one joint at a time. |
| The servo switched off by itself                               | The World may have been stopped or reset; stopping a World resets its robots' poses. Switch the servo on again.                                                                                     |
| The camera gateway shows no picture                            | The camera name equals the camera's prim name; the World plays and declares its cameras                                                                                                             |
| The robot moves slower than expected                           | In Theater, **Physics RTF** is below 1.00: the World simulates slower than real time ([Theater](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/theater/index.md))                                |
# Run and Monitor

# Start and Monitor Nodes

Nodes run only on the Live page, and only when you start them. This page covers starting and stopping nodes, reading their state and logs, and what to do when a node does not start.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Go Live

Open the Robot System with **Station · Edit** and click **Go live**, or activate it on the project page and open **Station · Live** ([Edit and Live](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/overview/#edit-and-live)). The Station comes up with its saved graph, documents and apps, but **no node starts by itself**: nodes that have not run yet show **Planned**.

Starting and stopping nodes needs the **Can edit** or **Can manage** role in the project.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Start All Nodes

Click **Start all nodes** in the toolbar. The Station starts every node that is not running, in dependency order: *Nodes start in dependency order: gateway → controller → compound → application.* A node waits until the nodes it requires are up.

- A banner follows the progress. **Cancel start** stops the run; nodes that already started stay up.
- The result shows as a banner: *Runtime topology is up.*, or *Runtime topology is up; stopped during startup: …* when some nodes stopped again ([Troubleshooting](#6-troubleshooting)).
- The arrow next to the button opens its menu: **Start all nodes** and **Stop all nodes**.
- *Nothing in this topology can be launched from here.* means that the graph holds only empty drafts.

**Run** on the project page does the same for a Robot System, and can start a World and several Stations in one step ([Run and Stop](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#2-run-and-stop)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Start, Restart or Stop One Node

Right-click a node on the Live page:

The menu of a running node

| Item                            | Shown when                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Open …**                      | The node has a UI of its own, for example Strider or Motion Studio                                          |
| **Start node**                  | The node is not running                                                                                     |
| **Restart node**, **Stop node** | The node runs                                                                                               |
| **Delete node**                 | Always ([Rename and Delete](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/graph/#4-rename-and-delete)) |

Start a robot's nodes in order: the gateway first, then its controller, then the nodes that use the controller. Stop them in the reverse order.

The operator UIs that open from nodes are described in [Strider](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/strider/index.md), [Motion Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/motion_studio/index.md) and [Articulation](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/articulation/index.md).

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Node States

The footer of each node card and the inspector header show the node's state, and the inspector adds a short description.

| State                              | Description                              |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| **Planned**                        | *Not started yet.*                       |
| **Booting**, **Starting**          | *Starting up.*                           |
| **Waiting binding**                | *A required port has no connection yet.* |
| **Waiting target**                 | *Connected target is not ready yet.*     |
| **Ready**                          | *Started and waiting to operate.*        |
| **Operating**                      | *Running normally.*                      |
| **Running**, **Active**            | *Process is up.*                         |
| **Paused**                         | *Paused.*                                |
| **Idle**                           | *Instance exists but is not running.*    |
| **Degraded**                       | *Running with reduced performance.*      |
| **Disconnected**                   | *Heartbeat lost.*                        |
| **Fault**                          | *Fault state — reset to recover.*        |
| **Error**, **Failed**, **Crashed** | *The node reported an error.*            |
| **Stopped**, **Exited**            | *Process ended.*                         |

The dot next to the state is green while the node runs, yellow while it waits, red for errors and grey otherwise. Problems are also counted in the **N issues** chip of the toolbar.

**Waiting binding** means that the node runs, but a port it requires is not connected to a running node that provides it. Connect the port, and start the providing node first: the gateway before its controller. When the two ports do not fit together, the inspector shows the reason instead of the description.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Logs and Activity

On the Live page, the **Logs** section of the inspector shows the node's latest output. Choose a stream and click **Refresh**:

| Stream                                  | Contents                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Package log**                         | The app's own log                                                                                        |
| **Standard output**, **Standard error** | The program's output                                                                                     |
| **Node log (userdata)**                 | The node's log file                                                                                      |
| **Process log**                         | When the process started and stopped                                                                     |
| **Gateway events**                      | A gateway's status and problems. A controller shows the events of its gateway as **Gateway events (…)**. |

Each stream shows its last 200 lines and when it was last updated, for example *Last 200 lines · updated 5 s ago*.

- *Station packages are still being restored; this node may not start yet.* The Station is still installing its apps after going live. Wait a moment, then start the node.
- *Package restore at Station start failed: …* The node's app could not be installed ([Apps and Packages](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/apps/index.md)).

**Activity**, under the logs, lists the latest changes to the node and who made them. The **Notifications** bell in the left rail lists the Station's recent events: nodes added, connected and deleted, files uploaded, and on the Live page also nodes started and stopped, and errors.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Troubleshooting

| Message                                                                                        | What to do                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| *… did not start: …*                                                                           | The app ended at once; the text after the colon is its own reason. **Details** shows more, and **Copy** copies it. Fix the cause, often the document or a setting, then start again. |
| *… cannot start yet: connect the … port or set …*                                              | The app needs that port connected, or that parameter set in **Parameters**. Do one of the two, then start again.                                                                     |
| *Install the package of … (…) from the Store first. Nothing was started.*                      | The node's app is not installed on this Station ([Apps and Packages](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/apps/index.md))                                              |
| *Provider not ready: …* or *Requirements never bound*                                          | A node that it requires did not come up. Start that node first and read its log.                                                                                                     |
| *Process exited before reaching readiness* or *Timed out waiting for readiness*                | The node stopped or hung while starting. Read its logs.                                                                                                                              |
| *Process stopped during topology startup; check its logs before retrying.*                     | The node started, then stopped. Read its logs, fix the cause, then start again.                                                                                                      |
| *Gateway … cannot be driven by both … and …; choose one controller before starting all nodes.* | Two controllers are connected to one gateway. Disconnect one of them.                                                                                                                |
| *Project edit access is required to start or cancel the topology.*                             | Your role is **Can view**. Ask a manager for **Can edit**.                                                                                                                           |

A gateway that cannot reach its robot in the World does not fail: it waits. See [Connect to the World](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/world_connection/#7-troubleshooting).

______________________________________________________________________

## 7. Stop

| To               | Do this                                                                                                                                     | The Station                                                                               |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Stop one node    | Right-click it › **Stop node**                                                                                                              | Stays live                                                                                |
| Stop every node  | Choose **Stop all nodes** in the menu of **Start all nodes** (users of a node stop before the node itself), or **Stop** on the project page | Stays live and keeps using credits                                                        |
| End your session | **Stop live** in the Station, or **Deactivate** on the project page                                                                         | Stops every node, saves its data and returns to the Edit page. It no longer uses credits. |

**Stop live** and **Deactivate** do the same. If nobody uses an active Station, Auto off deactivates it after 30 minutes by default ([Auto Off](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#5-auto-off)).

Stopping this Station does not stop or deactivate its World, and does not end separate rendering sessions. End those from the project page and close unneeded views.

# Theater

Theater shows an active Robot World live in your browser: the simulation as it runs, the robots in it and the Stations that drive them. Its browser tab is titled *Cosmic Theater*.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Open Theater

1. Activate the World on the project page ([Activate and Run](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/index.md)).
1. Click **Theater** in the World's **Actions** column. The link is available once the World is **Active** and its live view is ready.
1. In **Choose rendering mode**, pick **RTX Real-time** or **WebGPU** and click **Open Cosmic Theater** ([Choose Rendering Mode](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#choose-rendering-mode)). Theater opens in a new tab.
1. From Studio, **Enter Theater** activates the World if needed and opens it here ([Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/studio/#7-enter-theater)).
1. While the World loads, Theater shows the progress, including **Robot cameras** when the World has cameras. The first time a scene opens in **RTX Real-time**, the renderer prepares it, which can take several minutes.
1. Opening Theater does not play the World: **Run** on the project page or **Start Theater** plays it ([Start and Stop](#start-and-stop)).
1. Watching counts as use of the World: an active World that nobody watches in Theater is deactivated by Auto off after 30 minutes.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. The Theater Window

| Area             | What it holds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Header**       | The project and World names; the status, *Ready* once the World is shown; the renderer menu (**RTX Real-time** ▾ or **WebGPU** ▾); a timer; **Start Theater** or **Stop Theater**; **Resources** ▾; **Share** (link icon); the **Active users** who are watching                   |
| **Scene assets** | The top levels of the World, with **Search assets** and the number of assets. **Hide panel** folds it away.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Viewport**     | The running World. **Perspective** ▾ holds camera presets (Perspective, Top, Bottom, Front, Back, Left, Right). **View** ▾ holds **Grid**, **Quality** (resolution and frame rate), **Fit** and **Presentation mode**, which shows the viewport full screen until you press `Esc`. |
| **Readout**      | At the bottom of the viewport, for example *1920x1080 · 60 FPS · Physics RTF 1.00*                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Runtime**      | The Station that drives the selected robot ([Select a Robot](#4-select-a-robot))                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

**Physics RTF** is the real-time factor of the simulation: simulated time divided by wall-clock time, measured over about five seconds. At 1.00 the simulation keeps up with real time; *—* means there is no fresh measurement. **FPS** is the rate at which the picture is drawn.

The renderer menu switches your view to the other rendering mode. The current picture stays until the new one is ready. The choice applies to your view only; the simulation is the same for everyone.

### Start and Stop

**Start Theater** plays the World's simulation and **Stop Theater** stops it. One viewer controls them: the first person with edit access who opened Theater. For the others, the button is dimmed and they watch. Members with **Can view** always watch. While the World is not playing, viewers who watch see the status *Ready · Paused*.

Theater plays and stops only the simulation; it does not start or stop any Station. **Run** and **Stop** on the project page act on the files you select there, the World and its Stations alike ([Activate and Run](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#2-run-and-stop)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Move the Camera

The camera moves as in Studio: right-drag to look around, the wheel to move closer or farther, middle-drag to pan and `Alt` + left-drag to orbit ([Keys and Camera](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/studio/#6-keys-and-camera)). Each viewer has their own camera.

| Key       | Action                                                                             |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `F`       | Frame the selection, or the whole World when nothing is selected                   |
| `Shift+F` | Follow the selection. A *Tracking* chip appears; **Stop** on it ends the tracking. |
| `Esc`     | Stop following; leave presentation mode                                            |

Right-click a row in **Scene assets** for **Focus** and **Focus and Track**.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Select a Robot

1. Click a robot in the viewport, or its row in **Scene assets**. Double-click the row to bring the camera to the robot.
1. In **RTX Real-time**, a card appears above the robot with its name and **Open Station**, followed by the Robot System that drives it. In both modes, right-clicking the robot's row in **Scene assets** offers **Open Station** as well.
1. **Open Station** opens that Robot System's live Station in a new tab. Members with **Can view** get a page they can only look at.

The **Runtime** dock opens on the right by itself when you select a robot that a Station drives. It shows that Station's graph, read-only, with the state of each node, so you can see at a glance whether the gateway and the controller are running.

- **Widen Runtime** makes the dock wider, and **Hide Runtime** closes it. **Show Runtime** in a row's right-click menu opens it again.
- The zoom buttons and **Fit view** at the bottom arrange the graph.
- When no Station drives the robot, the card or the menu says so, for example *No Station is running in this project.*

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Several Viewers

- Everyone who opens an active World watches the same simulation. **Active users** in the header shows who is watching.
- Each person chooses their own rendering mode and moves their own camera.
- Each viewer in **RTX Real-time** has a cloud renderer of their own, which uses credits. A viewer in **WebGPU** draws with their own computer's GPU, and your plan may still count that view ([Billing and Usage](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/billing/index.md)).
- **Share** shows the link to this Theater, and **Copy** copies it. The link opens for people who are signed in and have access to the project ([Share and Collaborate](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/sharing/index.md)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. What Theater Does Not Do

- It does not edit the World. Deactivate the World and open it in [Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/studio/index.md).
- It does not start or stop Stations; use **Run** and **Stop** on the project page, or the Station itself.
- It has no recording or screenshot button. To capture the view, use your operating system's screenshot or screen-recording tools.

______________________________________________________________________

## 7. Troubleshooting

| Message                                                          | What to do                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| *Unable to load World*, with a reason                            | Click **Retry**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| *No saved World yet*                                             | The World has no scene. Deactivate it, build the scene in Studio and save it.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| *Preparing the RTX renderer*                                     | The first time a scene opens in **RTX Real-time**, the renderer prepares it. Wait; this can take several minutes.                                                                                                                                |
| *RTX needs free GPU resources. …*                                | The cloud GPUs are busy. Wait, or close Theater and open it again in **WebGPU**.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| *The World did not finish loading in 3 minutes. …*               | The World is very large, or the renderer cannot open it. Click **Retry**; if it fails again, make the World lighter ([Prepare a World for Simulation](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/prepare_world/#6-keep-the-world-light)). |
| *Physics connection failed, retrying*                            | Wait: Theater retries by itself.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| *Your sign-in expired. Open this World again from Sodero Cloud.* | Open Theater again from the project page.                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| *No Station is running in this project.*                         | No Robot System of the project is active. Activate the one that drives the robot.                                                                                                                                                                |
| **Start Theater** is dimmed                                      | Another viewer controls the simulation, or your role is **Can view**.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| *View access: you can look but not change this project.*         | Your role is **Can view**. Ask a manager for **Can edit**.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
# Operate Robots

# Strider

**Strider** is the operator UI for wheeled mobile bases. With it you jog the base, watch its state and odometry, and send navigation goals. It works with every drive type that a mobile robot document (`.sddm`) can describe: differential drive, skid steer 4WD, mecanum 4WD, swerve 4WD and Ackermann.

______________________________________________________________________

## How Strider Works in a Station

Two nodes are involved:

| Node                | Role                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sodero.mlc.<name>` | The mobile base controller. It turns body velocities into wheel commands for its gateway, integrates odometry, and keeps the speed and acceleration limits of its `.sddm` document. It has no UI of its own.                |
| `sodero.strider`    | Strider. It drives what its ports are connected to: `mobile_base` to the base controller (driving and status), `localization` to the localizer (the robot's position on the map) and `navigation` to the navigator (goals). |

```
flowchart LR
    S["sodero.strider"] -- mobile_base --> M["sodero.mlc.jackal<br>jackal.sddm"]
    M -- servo_link --> G["sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal<br>jackal.gw"]
    S -. localization .-> L["sodero.icp_localizer"]
    S -. navigation .-> N["sodero.navigator"]
```

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Set Up the Nodes

1. In the Station's **Store**, install `sodero.actuator_gateway`, `sodero.mlc` and `sodero.strider` ([Apps and Packages](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/apps/index.md)).
1. Add the gateway, the base controller and Strider. Connect the controller's `servo_link` to the gateway, and Strider's `mobile_base` to the base controller ([Build the Graph](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/graph/index.md)).
1. Upload the gateway's `.gw` and the controller's `.sddm` document ([Documents and Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/documents/index.md)).
1. Set the gateway's **Robot name** and check the actuator mapping ([Connect to the World](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/world_connection/index.md)).
1. Run the World, go live, then start the gateway, the controller and Strider, in this order ([Start and Monitor Nodes](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/run/index.md)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Open Strider

On the Live page, right-click the running `sodero.strider` node and choose **Open …** ([Start and Monitor Nodes](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/run/#3-start-restart-or-stop-one-node)). Strider opens in a new tab. If its session expires, open it again from the node.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Screen Layout

The left rail has three pages: **Status**, **Drive** and **Navigation**. The top bar holds the actions of the current page and, on every page:

| Item             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Readiness pill   | The current state in one line, for example *Manual Drive Ready* or *Servo Off*. Click it for the checks: Connection, Mobile base, Servo, Localization, Navigation.                                 |
| **System Log**   | Events of this browser session, filtered by System, Drive, Navigation and Localization                                                                                                             |
| **Motion Alarm** | Active alarms and recent errors                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **E-STOP**       | Software stop: cancels driving and the navigation goal and sets the wheel speeds to zero at once, with the servo still on. It latches until **Clear E-Stop**, which switches the base to **Idle**. |
| Units            | `m / m/s / deg` or `m / m/s / rad`, for display only                                                                                                                                               |

### Status Page

| Card                           | Contents                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Trajectory (Odometry View)** | The path driven since the last mode change, in the odometry frame                          |
| **Operation Status**           | Ready, moving or idle, servo on or off, and faults or stops                                |
| **Base Status (Odometry)**     | Mode, and X, Y, Theta, VX, VY, WZ                                                          |
| **Control Node Health**        | Whether the base, the localizer and the navigator are reachable                            |
| **Drive Unit Status**          | The drive template and, per wheel, the servo state, position, velocity and target velocity |
| **Recent Events**              | The latest events; **View All** opens the **System Log**                                   |

**Watchdog Tripped** while the base stands still in **Twist** mode is normal: no velocity command is arriving, so the base holds zero speed.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Jog the Base

On the **Drive** page:

1. Under **Drive Mode**, click **Twist**.
1. Under **Servo / Safety**, switch **Servo On**. The readiness pill shows *Manual Drive Ready*.
1. Set the **Linear Velocity Limit** (0.2 m/s by default, at most 0.8 m/s) and the **Angular Velocity Limit**.
1. Press and hold a pad button: **Forward (W)**, **Backward (S)**, **Turn Left (A)** or **Turn Right (D)**. The base moves while you hold the button and stops when you release it; **Stop (Space)** stops it too.
1. To drive with the keyboard, switch on **Live** in **Manual Drive**, then use **W**, **S**, **A**, **D** and **Space**. Commands stop when the window loses focus.
1. When you are done, switch the servo off and click **Idle**.

| Control                | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Drive Mode**         | **Idle**: no motion. **Twist**: body velocity commands, for jogging and navigation. **Wheel**: direct wheel speeds (advanced). **EMG**: stops the base like **E-STOP**, without latching. |
| **Servo On** / **Off** | Enables or disables the drives. **Fault Reset** clears drive faults; then switch the servo off and on again.                                                                              |
| **Stop Motion**        | Stops manual driving and cancels a navigation goal                                                                                                                                        |

Manual commands take priority over navigation: jogging during a navigation goal overrides the navigator and can end the goal. A manual command expires after about a second, so the base stops if the connection drops. A navigation goal does not expire: cancel it with **Stop Motion**, **Cancel** or **E-STOP**.

**Show** next to **Advanced Controls** opens **Wheel Direct** (each wheel's speed in **Wheel** mode), **Preview Command** (the wheel speeds a body velocity would give, without moving), **Steering Origin**, **Calibration** and **Record / Replay**.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Navigation Page

The **Navigation** page works when Strider's `localization` and `navigation` ports are connected to a running localizer and navigator, and the Station has a map bundle. To set them up, install `sodero.icp_localizer` and `sodero.navigator` from the Store, connect the localizer's `camera` port to the robot's camera gateway and the navigator's `mobile_base` and `localization` ports to the base controller and the localizer, and upload the map bundle ([Build the Graph › Common Connections](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/graph/#common-connections), [Documents and Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/documents/#2-kinds-of-documents)).

| Card                                                                         | Contents                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Navigation Map (Occupancy Grid)**                                          | The map, the robot, the planned path and the goal. Drag to pan, scroll to zoom.                                       |
| **Localization Status**                                                      | Healthy, Degraded, Initializing, Relocalizing, Lost or Uninitialized. **Global localization** searches the whole map. |
| **Mission Status**, **Current Pose (Map)**, **Goal Pose**, **Route Summary** | The goal, where the robot is and how far it still has to go                                                           |
| **Navigator**                                                                | The navigator's state and a **Speed Limit** slider (10–100 %)                                                         |
| **Navigation Controls**                                                      | **Set Initial Pose**, **Set Goal**, **Clear Goal**, **Pause**, **Resume**, **Cancel**                                 |

### Set the Initial Pose

If the localization status is not **Healthy**:

1. Click **Set Initial Pose**.
1. Press on the map where the robot stands and drag in the direction it faces.
1. Click **Set initial pose** (or **Relocalize here** when a pose was set before).

### Send a Goal

1. Make sure the base is in **Twist** with the servo on: the readiness pill shows *Navigation Ready*.
1. Click **Set Goal**, press on the map where the robot should go and drag in the direction it should face.
1. Click **Start Navigation**. The planned path appears.

**Pause** cancels the goal and keeps it; **Resume** sends it again. **Cancel** stops navigation.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Control Strider from Programs

- **AI agents** drive the base with the `station.strider` tools: state, servo, velocities, stops and fault reset ([AI Agents](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/ai_agents/index.md)).
- **Your own module** on the Station connects to the base controller's `mobile_base` port ([Apps and Packages](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/apps/index.md)).
- **Your own tools** on your computer reach the Station API through the [Project VPN](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/project_vpn/index.md).

# Motion Studio

**Motion Studio** is the operator UI for manipulators. The manipulator controller node, `sodero.mmc.<name>`, runs the arm's real-time controller: kinematics, dynamics, trajectory generation and safety limits, from the arm's `.sdd` document. Motion Studio belongs to that node. It shows the arm in 3D, jogs it, defines tools and teaches poses.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Set Up the Nodes

1. In the Station's **Store**, install `sodero.actuator_gateway` and `sodero.mmc` ([Apps and Packages](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/apps/index.md)).
1. Add the gateway and the manipulator controller, and connect the controller's `servo_link` to the gateway ([Build the Graph](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/graph/index.md)).
1. Upload the gateway's `.gw` and the controller's `.sdd` document ([Documents and Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/documents/index.md)).
1. Set the gateway's **Robot name** and check the actuator mapping ([Connect to the World](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/world_connection/index.md)).
1. Run the World, go live, then start the gateway and the controller, in this order ([Start and Monitor Nodes](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/run/index.md)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Open Motion Studio

On the Live page, right-click the running `sodero.mmc.<name>` node and choose **Open …** ([Start and Monitor Nodes](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/run/#3-start-restart-or-stop-one-node)). Motion Studio opens in a new tab. If its session expires, open it again from the node.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Screen Layout

| Item                   | Description                                                                                  |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Pages                  | **Home**, **Tool** and **Pose**                                                              |
| 3D view                | The arm in its current pose, with the 3D model of its `.sdd`                                 |
| **Joint Status**       | Per joint: position, target position, velocity, target velocity, effort and residual effort  |
| **TCP Status**         | Position and orientation of the tool center point (TCP), and its linear and angular velocity |
| **Active Tool Status** | The active tool's TCP offset, center of mass and payload mass                                |
| **Filters**            | Shows or hides the cards of the Home page                                                    |

### Header

| Item                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Robot and role        | The controller node, and whether this window has control (*Pilot - Control Active*)                                                                                                               |
| **Manual** / **Auto** | **Manual** limits the linear speed of the TCP in the controller's own motions and jogs, 0.25 m/s by default; it does not limit rotations or **Hand** mode. **Auto** runs at the programmed speed. |
| Feed rate             | Speed override in percent (10–150 %), applied to motion in progress                                                                                                                               |
| **Error Reset**       | Clears a protective stop (a joint at its limit, a speed or torque limit, a detected collision) and resets drive faults. Switch the servo on again afterwards.                                     |
| Units                 | `mm / g / deg` or `m / kg / radian`                                                                                                                                                               |
| **Jog**               | Opens the jog panel                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **Command log**       | Commands sent from this window                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Alarm**             | Active alarms and notifications                                                                                                                                                                   |

The mark at the top left opens the menu, with **File** to import and export tools and poses.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Jog the Arm

Click **Jog** in the header to open the jog panel.

1. Switch **Servo On**.
1. In **JOG OPTION**, choose the **Mode**:
   - **Joint**: move one joint at a time (J1…Jn).
   - **Base**: move the tool in the robot's base frame (X, Y, Z, RX, RY, RZ).
   - **Tool**: move the tool in its own frame.
   - **Hand**: hand guiding, for a real arm. The arm compensates gravity and the jog buttons are disabled.
1. Choose **Continuous** (moves while you hold a button) or **Step** (5° or 10 mm per click), and the **Speed**: 50 %, 100 % or 150 %, about 0.04, 0.1 and 0.2 m/s at the tool.
1. Hold **−** or **+** next to a joint or axis in **JOG CONTROL**. The motion stops when you release the button.

The **POSE** section of the panel shows the current TCP pose and joint positions.

**Stop the motion before you leave the UI.** A continuous jog stops when the release of the button reaches the controller. If the browser or the connection fails while you jog, do not assume that the arm has stopped: stop the controller node in the Station and check in Theater that the arm stands still. For a real arm, see [Stop Controls](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/latest/hardware_setup/stop_controls/) in the Stellar X manual.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Tools

The **Tool** page defines the tools mounted on the flange.

1. Click **+** to add a tool, and rename it with the pencil icon, for example `gripper`.
1. Enter the **TOOL CENTER POINT**: the TCP position and orientation relative to the flange. The calculator icon opens **TCP Calibration**, which computes the TCP from 3–10 poses that touch the same point.
1. Enter the **PAYLOAD PROPERTIES**: center of mass, inertia and mass. The calculator icon opens **Payload Calibration**.
1. Click **Save**, or **Save and Apply** to make it the active tool at once. **Set as active tool** activates a saved tool.

A wrong payload makes hand guiding and collision detection unreliable. Set the mass and center of mass of every tool you mount.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Poses

The **Pose** page stores named poses.

1. Jog the arm to the pose, then click the camera icon (**Save Current Pose**). Or click **+** (**Add pose**) and fill in the values.
1. Select the pose in the list. **POSE DATA** shows its TCP pose and joint positions; **Set from current** copies the current pose into it.
1. Under **TEST MOVE**, choose **Joint** or **Linear** motion and hold **Hold to move**. The arm moves to the pose only while you hold the button.
1. Click **Save**.

Saved poses appear as markers in the 3D view. Right-click a pose to copy, duplicate or delete it. **File** in the menu exports and imports tools and poses.

______________________________________________________________________

## 7. Program the Arm

Motion Studio is for setup and teaching. Programs run outside it and use the same controller:

| From            | How                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| AI agents       | The `station.motion` tools: state, servo, moves, stops and fault reset ([AI Agents](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/ai_agents/index.md))        |
| Your own module | A module node on the Station, connected to the manipulator controller node ([Apps and Packages](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/apps/index.md)) |
| Your own tools  | The Station API, through the [Project VPN](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/project_vpn/index.md)                                                |

**From simulation to a real arm.** The arm's `.sdd` document, its tools and poses, and your programs carry over to a real arm on Stellar X, which uses an EtherCAT gateway instead of the simulation gateway. A real arm needs its own checks first: see [Motion Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/latest/controllers/motion_studio/) in the Stellar X manual.

# Articulation

The **Articulation** controller drives an articulated robot joint by joint: legged robots, humanoids, grippers, pan-tilt heads, or any set of joints that receives joint targets. Unlike the manipulator controller, it uses no arm kinematics (no DH parameters, no Cartesian motions). It bounds and forwards the joint targets of an upper controller, such as a walking policy in your own module, and its **Articulation** UI lets you jog the joints by hand.

| Item     | Value                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Node     | `sodero.amc.<name>`                                                                                                                                               |
| Document | `.sdda`, made in Stellar Designer ([Articulated Robot](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/latest/tutorials/stellar_designer/articulation/) in the Stellar X manual) |
| Joints   | 1 to 64, driven by one actuator gateway                                                                                                                           |
| Units    | rad, rad/s, N·m                                                                                                                                                   |

```
flowchart LR
    U["Upper controller<br>your module"] -- "joint targets" --> A["Articulation<br>sodero.amc.dog"]
    A -- servo_link --> G["Actuator gateway<br>sodero.actuator_gateway.dog"]
```

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. The Document

An `.sdda` document lists the joints and how the gateway's actuators drive them.

| Per joint          | Meaning                                                    |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Name               | Joint name                                                 |
| Position min / max | Range of motion; targets outside it are refused            |
| Velocity max       | Velocity limit, also the reference for the jog speed       |
| Torque max         | Torque limit; the controller clamps its total output to it |
| Offset (optional)  | Joint position at actuator position zero                   |
| Kp, Kd (optional)  | Stiffness and damping, for PD torque control               |

- **Drive mode.** In `position` mode, the controller bounds the joint targets and the drive follows them with its own position control. In `pd_torque` mode, the controller computes a PD torque from Kp and Kd and sends torque commands.
- **Actuator mapping.** One actuator can move several joints, and several actuators can move one joint, as long as the mapping can be inverted.
- **Watchdogs.** The controller switches the servo off and latches a stop when the gateway's feedback is older than 100 ms, or when no new target arrives for 200 ms (the defaults). Click **Clear stop**, then **Servo on**. Reconnecting never switches the servo on by itself.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Set Up the Nodes

1. In the Station's **Store**, install `sodero.actuator_gateway` and `sodero.amc` ([Apps and Packages](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/apps/index.md)).
1. Add the gateway and the Articulation controller, and connect the controller's `servo_link` to the gateway ([Build the Graph](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/graph/index.md)).
1. Upload the gateway's `.gw` and the controller's `.sdda` document ([Documents and Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/documents/index.md)).
1. Set the gateway's **Robot name** and check the actuator mapping ([Connect to the World](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/world_connection/index.md)).
1. Run the World, go live, then start the gateway, the controller and the program that sends joint targets, in this order ([Start and Monitor Nodes](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/run/index.md)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Open the Articulation UI

On the Live page, right-click the running `sodero.amc.<name>` node and choose **Open …** ([Start and Monitor Nodes](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/run/#3-start-restart-or-stop-one-node)). The Articulation UI opens in a new tab. If its session expires, open it again from the node.
