| Area              | Contents                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Left rail         | **Joints** (joint monitor), **Constraints** (the configured limits), **Set origin**                                                                                                                             |
| Top bar           | **Servo on**, **Servo off**, **Stop** (switches the servo off and latches a stop), **Clear stop** (releases it while the servo is off), the control mode, and the button that opens the **Joint control** panel |
| Status strip      | **Servo** on or off, **Feedback** age in milliseconds, **Safety** (*Ready* or the reason for a stop)                                                                                                            |
| **Controller**    | The Articulation node this window controls                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Joint monitor** | Per joint: position, velocity, effort and target                                                                                                                                                                |

**Stop the upper controller first.** Pause or stop the program that sends joint targets, such as a walking policy, before you jog the joints by hand.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Jog Joints

1. Open the **Joint control** panel with the button at the right of the top bar.
1. Click **Servo on**.
1. Under **Joint jog**, set the **Speed**: 1–100 % of each joint's velocity limit, 10 % by default.
1. Hold **−** or **+** next to a joint. The joint moves while you hold the button and holds its position when you release it. A jog button also switches the servo on if it is off.

Leaving the window, switching to another tab or losing the connection switches the servo off.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Send Joint Targets

Under **Joint targets**:

1. Click **Use measured positions** to copy the current positions into the target fields.
1. Change the targets of the joints you want to move.
1. Click **Stream targets**. The controller follows the targets while the stream runs; **Stop target stream** ends it and switches the servo off.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Set the Origin

**Set origin** gives the current position of a joint a known angle, for example after an encoder was replaced on a real robot. Robots in a Robot World do not support it. For real robots, see [Articulation](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/latest/controllers/articulation/) in the Stellar X manual.

______________________________________________________________________

## 7. Control from Programs

| From            | How                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A walking robot | Your module runs the walking policy and sends joint targets to the Articulation node                                                                                      |
| AI agents       | The `station.articulation` tools: state, servo, joint targets, stops and fault reset ([AI Agents](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/ai_agents/index.md)) |
| Your own tools  | The Station API, through the [Project VPN](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/project_vpn/index.md)                                                       |
# Connect and Automate

# Project VPN

The Project VPN connects a device of yours, such as your computer or a robot PC, to the Stations of a project, so you can use a Station's API from a terminal, your own scripts or your IDE. You approve every connection yourself, and a connection lasts at most 8 hours.

**AI agents don't need the Project VPN.** To work on a project with Claude Code or another AI agent, see [AI Agents](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/ai_agents/index.md).

______________________________________________________________________

## What the Project VPN Reaches

A connection reaches each Station (Robot System) of the project that was active when you connected: its API on port 8001, and the extra TCP ports opened for it ([VPN Ports](#4-vpn-ports)). It does not reach Robot Worlds, Stations activated or restarted after you connected, or other projects. Your device can call a Station, but a Station cannot connect to your device.

The Project VPN doesn't start anything: activate the Stations you want to use first ([Activate and Run](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/index.md)). An active Station uses credits whether or not you are connected, and your tools' calls to it count as use for [Auto off](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#5-auto-off).

The project's owner and people with **Can manage** can connect devices and copy Station API keys. When your role doesn't allow it, the panel says *Your project role can't use the Project VPN. Ask the project owner for access.*

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Install Connector

Install the Connector once on each device you want to connect. It adds the `sodero` command, which connects the device.

1. Open the project and click **Project VPN** in the top bar.
1. Expand **Install Connector**. It shows an install command for **Linux**, **macOS** and **Windows** in two groups:
   - **Desktop PC**, for a computer with a desktop;
   - **Robot or server PC (headless)**, for a device without a desktop: the command installs without prompts and starts no tray app.
1. Copy the command for the device's system and run it on the device: on Linux or macOS in a terminal, as your normal user; on Windows in PowerShell. Approve the administrator prompt.
1. Sign in once on the device: run `sodero login`. It opens the Sodero sign-in in your browser; without a desktop, it prints the sign-in address and explains how to open it. Finish within 5 minutes.

The Project VPN panel of Warehouse Demo

The command checks the installer before it runs it. On Linux, the installer supports Debian and Ubuntu. On Windows, it also installs WireGuard for Windows, which the Connector uses. Your system lists the Connector as **Sodero VPN**; on a desktop PC it also adds an optional status icon (**Sodero VPN** in your app menu, or `sodero tray`).

This `sodero` command belongs to the Connector. It is not the [sodero CLI](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/latest/ssh_workspace/sodero_cli/) of the Stellar X SSH workspace.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Connect a Device

Every device connects the same way, this computer included.

1. Activate at least one Station of the project. In **Project VPN**, click **Connect a device**. A new row shows the steps and the command for the device, `sodero vpn connect '…'`, with a link in it.
1. Click **Copy** next to the command, then run the command on the device and keep it running. The link works once, for one device, and only for 60 seconds (*Link expires in … · one device*); **Get a new link** replaces it.
1. The command shows the project, the device and a six-character **Confirmation code**. Check that the code matches the one in the portal row, type `y` at *Connect this device to this project? [y/N]*, then type the code when the command asks for it.
1. The row shows **Connected**. **Details** lists the Stations in this connection.

The device must be approved within 5 minutes after you click **Connect a device**. When a request ends before the device connected, the row says *Ended before the device connected: …*; click **Connect a device** again.

**Approve only a connection you started.** If the portal shows a code that differs from the one on your device, another device used the link: cancel it in the portal and don't approve it.

**Keep the command running.** The device holds the connection: `Ctrl+C` or closing the terminal disconnects it. Once the row says *Connected — the device manages this connection.*, you can close the portal tab. To keep the connection after you log out of an SSH session, run the command inside `tmux` or `screen`.

`sodero vpn status` shows the connection, `sodero vpn disconnect` ends it, and `sodero --help` lists all commands.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Use a Station's Address and API Key

Each Station has its own address on the Project VPN. It stays the same when the Station is deactivated and activated again. You find it under **Station addresses** in the **Project VPN** panel and in the **IP address** column of the project's Robot Systems.

1. Connect your device while the Station is active.
1. Click the copy icon next to the Station's address. It copies `http://ADDRESS:8001/`.
1. Click the key icon (*Copy the Station's API key*). The key is copied to your clipboard; it is never shown on screen.
1. In your tools, use the address and send the key with each request. The message that confirms the copy names the request header to use.

**The key changes each time the Station starts.** After the Station is deactivated and activated again, connect again and copy the new key.

**Keep the key private.** Treat it like a password: don't paste it into shared documents and don't commit it with your code.

### Addresses for a Control Station

A control app that runs on one of the project's Stations reaches the other Stations at their **address inside the cloud**, which your devices can't reach. It changes when the Station restarts.

- The network icon next to a Station copies its address inside the cloud.
- **Copy for a control Station** copies one line for each running Station: its name, its address inside the cloud and its API key.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. VPN Ports

Besides its API port 8001, a Station can open more TCP ports on the Project VPN, for example for a service of your own module.

1. In **Station addresses**, click the **VPN ports** button (sliders icon) next to the Station. The dialog **VPN ports — *name*** opens.
1. Under **Extra TCP ports**, enter the ports, for example `9000, 9001`, and click **Save**.
1. You can open up to 16 TCP ports from 1024 to 65535. The dialog names the ports that the Station uses itself; they are refused.
1. The ports apply the next time the Station starts (*VPN ports saved. They apply the next time the Station starts.*). **Open now** lists the ports of the current run. A connected device must connect again to use newly opened ports.
1. Only the project's owner and people with **Can manage** can change VPN ports. Others see them read-only.
1. One connection carries at most 64 Station ports. In a project with many Stations, each Station's API port comes first, and some extra ports may be left out.

**Protect the services on extra ports.** Anyone with an approved connection to the project can reach these ports: the services on them must check their own sign-in.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Disconnect

Click **Disconnect** in the device's row in the portal. On the device, press `Ctrl+C` where `sodero vpn connect` runs, or run `sodero vpn disconnect`. On a desktop PC, the status icon also has **Disconnect VPN**.

A connection also ends on its own after 8 hours; about a minute after the command that holds it stops, for example when the device sleeps; when all its Stations are deactivated or restarted; when you lose access to the project; or when your workspace has used its Project VPN time or data for the month. The Connector never reconnects on its own.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Update or Uninstall the Connector

To update, run the install command from **Install Connector** with `update` in place of `install`, then connect again. To uninstall, run `sodero uninstall` (add `--purge` to also remove the VPN settings and the device identity), or on Windows uninstall **Sodero VPN** in **Installed apps**. WireGuard for Windows stays installed.

______________________________________________________________________

## Limits

| What                          | Limit                                                        |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Open connections per person   | 3, across all your projects                                  |
| Connections per device        | 1 at a time                                                  |
| Length of a connection        | 8 hours                                                      |
| Link for **Connect a device** | 60 seconds, one device                                       |
| Approving a device            | Within 5 minutes                                             |
| Extra TCP ports per Station   | 16, from 1024 to 65535                                       |
| Station ports per connection  | 64                                                           |
| Monthly use                   | Project VPN time and data per workspace, as your plan allows |

**Billing & Usage** shows the Project VPN time and data used this month ([Billing and Usage](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/billing/index.md)). When they are used up, new connections are refused until the counters reset.

______________________________________________________________________

## Troubleshooting

| Message or symptom                                                   | What to do                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| *No running Station is available for this project.*                  | Activate at least one Station, then connect.                                                                           |
| *You have 3 connections, the maximum. …*                             | Disconnect a connection you don't need, here or in another project.                                                    |
| *The link expired. Get a new one to continue.*                       | Click **Get a new link** and run the new command on the device within 60 seconds.                                      |
| *The confirmation code did not match. This device was not approved.* | Click **Connect a device** again, run the new command, and type the code exactly as the command shows it.              |
| *Ended before the device connected: …*                               | The device was not approved within 5 minutes, or the command stopped. Click **Connect a device** again.                |
| A Station is missing, or *Some Stations stopped or changed. …*       | The Station was activated or restarted after you connected. Disconnect, then connect again.                            |
| *A local network or another VPN already routes a target address.*    | Disconnect the other VPN, or connect from a different network.                                                         |
| *Not signed in to Sodero …* or *Your Sodero sign-in has ended …*     | Run `sodero login` on the device.                                                                                      |
| A checksum, size or signature mismatch during installation           | Don't work around it. Copy the command from **Install Connector** again; if the mismatch remains, report it to Sodero. |

# AI Agents

Connect Claude Code or another AI agent to your Sodero account, then ask it in plain language to work on your projects. The agent reaches Sodero Cloud over the Internet with a sign-in of its own; it needs neither the [Project VPN](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/project_vpn/index.md) nor anything installed from Sodero.

- *"Which Stations and Worlds in Warehouse Demo are active?"*
- *"Activate the warehouse World and the jackal Station, then start them."*
- *"Why did a node on jackal stop? Show me its log."*

______________________________________________________________________

## How It Works

```
flowchart TB
    You(["You"]) --> Agent["AI agent<br>on your computer"]
    Agent -- "MCP, with its own sign-in" --> Cloud["Sodero Cloud"]
    Cloud --> Projects["The workspaces and projects of your account:<br>Robot Systems, Robot Worlds, files"]
```

- You register Sodero once in your agent, as a remote MCP server. The registration belongs to your account, not to one project.
- The agent signs in through your browser with your Sodero account, and on a consent page you allow it to access your account. It never sees your password, and you can revoke its access at any time.
- The agent never gets more than your own project roles allow.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Register Sodero in Your Agent

Open any project and click **AI agents** in the top bar. The **AI agents (MCP)** panel shows the address and ready-made settings for your agent, and what your project role allows.

The AI agents panel of Warehouse Demo

Click **Copy command** and run the command once in a terminal:

```
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user sodero 'https://app.sodero.io/project-access/mcp'
```

`--scope user` makes Sodero available in all your working folders.

The client must support remote MCP servers over Streamable HTTP and sign in through your browser (OAuth). Add a remote server with the address that **Copy address** copies:

```
https://app.sodero.io/project-access/mcp
```

For a client with a JSON list of servers, expand **Other MCP clients** in the panel and click **Copy configuration**. Don't enter a token or a client ID: the client registers itself and signs in through your browser.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Sign In and Allow Access

1. Start the sign-in. In Claude Code, start `claude`, type `/mcp`, select **sodero** and choose **Authenticate**. Other clients have a **Connect** or **Sign in** action.
1. Your browser opens the Sodero sign-in. Sign in with your **Sodero** account, not with the account of your AI provider.
1. The consent page *Allow … to connect?* shows the permissions the agent requested and says: *This agent can access all workspaces and projects available to your account, including those you gain access to later. Current membership and roles always apply.* Click **Allow access**, or **Cancel** to refuse.
1. Return to your agent: Sodero is connected.

There is nothing to select: the consent covers your account, and the agent can use every project in which you have a role, now and later. What the agent may do depends on the access its client requests, which the consent page shows:

| Requested permissions                                       | What the agent may do                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| *read project data*                                         | Read your projects: status, items, files and jobs. This is the access a client gets when it requests no other.     |
| *read project data and change project data or run commands* | Also make changes, such as uploading files, activating Stations and Worlds and running the Station and World tools |

**Approve only your own agent.** The consent page shows the name the agent gives itself; Sodero can't verify it. Allow access only right after you started the sign-in from your own agent.

**Changes also need a project role that allows them.** The project's owner and people with **Can manage** can change a project through an agent; people with **Can view** can only read. The **AI agents** panel of each project says what your role permits there.

A connection lasts up to 30 days. To renew it or change its access, sign the agent in again (in Claude Code, from `/mcp`), then [revoke](#review-and-revoke-agents) the entries you no longer need.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Tell the Agent Which Project to Use

Every request names a project. In the **AI agents** panel, click **Copy project link** and paste the link into your request, or give the project's name, for example *"List files in Warehouse Demo"*. When two projects have the same name, use `workspace/name`.

______________________________________________________________________

## What Agents Can Do

The agent works through Sodero's tools. Each tool name has three parts, for example `project.item.start`.

| Area                    | Tools                                                                                                                                                   | The agent can                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Account                 | `account.workspace.list`, `account.project.list`                                                                                                        | List your workspaces, and the projects it may use with read or write permission for each                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Projects and jobs       | `project.info.get`, `project.item.list`, `project.job.list`, `project.job.status`, `project.history.list`                                               | Read a project's Robot Systems and Robot Worlds with their states, its jobs, and the actions agents took in it. Listing the Trash needs **Can manage**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Run                     | `project.item.start`, `project.item.stop`, `project.job.start`, `project.job.cancel`                                                                    | Activate or stop up to 8 Stations and Worlds at once, or activate and start them as one job                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Items                   | `project.item.create`, `project.item.duplicate`, `project.item.rename`, `project.item.trash`, `project.item.restore`, `project.item.delete_permanently` | Create, duplicate, rename and trash Robot Systems and Robot Worlds. Restoring and permanently deleting from the Trash need **Can manage**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Workspaces and projects | `workspace.project.create`, `workspace.history.list`, `project.manage.copy`, `project.manage.trash`                                                     | Create a project in a workspace where you may create projects, and list those requests. Copying a project and moving it to the Trash need **Can manage**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Files                   | `project.file.list`, `project.file.download`, `project.asset.list`, `project.package.list`                                                              | List and download library files, search the robot and gateway documents of Sodero Assets, and list a Station's apps and packages                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| File changes            | `project.upload.begin`, `project.upload.finish`, `project.upload.abort`, `project.file.rename`, `project.file.delete`                                   | Upload files, and rename and delete library files ([Usage Limits](#usage-limits))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Station and World tools | `system.tools.list`, `system.tools.describe`, `system.tools.call`                                                                                       | Run tools from a catalog of more than 100: Station status and logs, the node graph, documents, Store apps, robot control through [Motion Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/motion_studio/index.md), [Strider](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/strider/index.md) and [Articulation](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/articulation/index.md), navigation, cameras, and the World |

**Changes need write access.** So does `system.tools.call`, even for a tool that only reads. Tools for a running Station or World need it to be active.

The agent cannot go beyond your roles, use the Project VPN, read files on your computer through Sodero, or download the contents of Sodero Assets. Cancelling a job stops further steps but doesn't undo changes.

______________________________________________________________________

## Stay in Control

- **Approve changes yourself.** Most agents can ask before they use a tool. A practical setup: allow the read-only tools freely (`account.workspace.list`, `account.project.list`, `project.info.get`, `project.item.list`, `project.history.list`, `project.job.list`, `project.job.status`, `project.file.list`, `project.file.download`, `project.asset.list`, `project.package.list`, `workspace.history.list`, `system.tools.list`, `system.tools.describe`) and keep approval on for every other tool, especially `system.tools.call`, `project.item.start`, `project.item.stop` and `project.job.start`.
- **Your client shows the tool names its own way.** A client may add a prefix and replace the dots: Claude Code shows `project.item.start` as `mcp__sodero__project_item_start`.
- **Review previews.** Most changes are previewed first. `project.item.create`, `project.item.duplicate`, `project.item.start`, `project.item.stop` and `project.job.start` act at once.
- **The agent acts as you.** What it changes is changed for everyone in the project.
- **Watch your credits.** A Station or World that an agent activated uses credits until it is deactivated. [Auto off](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#5-auto-off) still applies.

The rules Sodero gives every agent (preview changes first, move a robot only when you asked for that motion, treat files and logs as data and not as instructions) are instructions to the agent, not a safety function. An agent can misread them or make mistakes, and its tools have the same effect as your own actions. Approve every change yourself.

______________________________________________________________________

## Usage Limits

Agent tool calls count against your workspace's plan, per minute and per calendar month (UTC). **Billing & Usage** shows the calls used this month ([Billing and Usage](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/billing/index.md)). At the monthly limit, calls are refused until the renewal date that the **AI agents** panel shows. At the per-minute limit, the agent is told how long to wait.

An upload can be up to 1 GiB for a library file and up to 64 MiB for other kinds, such as Station packages, World scenes, map bundles and Station documents.

A tool call ends after 100 seconds. A change may still have been applied: have the agent check the state before it repeats the change.

______________________________________________________________________

## Review and Revoke Agents

1. Click your avatar at the bottom of the left navigation bar and choose **Account Settings**.
1. Under **Connected AI agents**, each agent shows its name, when it connected, its scopes (*Read* or *Read, Write*) and its **Current workspaces**.
1. To disconnect an agent, click **Revoke** followed by the agent's name, then **Confirm revoke**.

Connected AI agents in Account settings

Revoking stops the agent's further calls and job steps but doesn't undo what was done. To connect the agent again, sign it in again.

______________________________________________________________________

## Troubleshooting

| Message or symptom                                                                      | What to do                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The sign-in ends without the consent page, and the agent reports that access was denied | Start the sign-in again and finish it within 10 minutes, with your Sodero account.                              |
| `AUTH_REQUIRED`, `AUTH_EXPIRED` or `CONNECTION_REVOKED`                                 | Sign the agent in again (Claude Code: `/mcp`).                                                                  |
| `GRANT_MISSING`                                                                         | Your account no longer has access to that workspace or project. Ask a person who manages it to add you again.   |
| `NOT_FOUND` for a project                                                               | No project you can use matches the name or link. Check the name, or use `workspace/name` or the project link.   |
| `WRITE_NOT_GRANTED`                                                                     | The connection may only read. Connect the agent again with a client that requests write access.                 |
| `FORBIDDEN`                                                                             | Your project role does not allow this action. Ask a person who can manage the project.                          |
| `RENAMED`                                                                               | The agent called a tool by a former name. The message names the current tool: the agent calls that one instead. |
| `STATION_NOT_RUNNING` or `WORLD_NOT_RUNNING`                                            | Activate the Station or World first.                                                                            |
| `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`                                                                        | Your workspace reached its plan's limit for agent calls. The message says when to try again.                    |
# Reference

# Compatibility

Sodero Cloud and Stellar X share the robot-system concepts and the document types. Each product runs its own release of Stellar Station, so their Store apps, menus, node names and accepted document versions can differ.

## Robot Documents and Apps

Use gateway and robot documents (`.gw`, `.sdd`, `.sddm`, `.sdda`) made for the Station release you work with, such as the documents in **Sodero Assets**. The Station refuses a document in two cases:

- **An older format.** The message says that the file *uses an obsolete format*, or names an *Obsolete robot file* or an *Obsolete gateway filename* ([Documents in an Obsolete Format](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/documents/#documents-with-old-node-names)).
- **A robot document without `runtime.yaml`.** Robot documents (`.sdd`, `.sddm`, `.sdda`) must contain a `runtime.yaml` that names their controller. Without it, the message says *The robot document has no runtime.yaml naming its controller.*

Documents exported from a current Stellar Designer meet both rules: export older documents again and upload the new file. Do not edit the files inside a document to make a Station accept it.

Install the apps that your nodes run from the Station's **Store** before you start the nodes ([Apps and Packages](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/apps/index.md)).

## Move Files Between Products

An `.sdr` file carries a Robot System between Sodero Cloud and Stellar X, without its installed packages. Check the destination's Station release and apps before you import it ([Move Robot Systems Between Stellar X and Sodero Cloud](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/files/#move-robot-systems-between-stellar-x-and-sodero-cloud)).

The [Stellar X manual](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/latest/) describes the Station on the controller. Use it for the concepts and the device steps; this manual's menus, such as **Store**, **Station · Edit**, **Go live** and **Station · Live**, apply to Sodero Cloud.

## Example Files

- The [Quick Start](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/get_started/quick_start/index.md) scene `jackal_warehouse.zip` contains a Clearpath Jackal and a Clearpath Dingo with their license notice. Keep the license file with the scene when you pass it on.
- The Quick Start's `jackal.gw` and `jackal.sddm` are the simulation gateway document and the mobile robot document of that Jackal, made for the Station release of Sodero Cloud.

## Browser and Rendering

Use an up-to-date desktop browser. **WebGPU** needs support from the browser, the operating system and the GPU; when it is not available on your device, use **RTX Real-time**, which renders in the cloud and streams the picture ([Choose Rendering Mode](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#choose-rendering-mode)).

## External Tools

- **Project VPN:** install the Connector with the command for your operating system under **Install Connector** in the project's **Project VPN** panel, then sign in once with `sodero login` ([Project VPN](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/project_vpn/index.md)).
- **AI agents:** connect them with the address and settings of the project's **AI agents** panel ([AI Agents](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/ai_agents/index.md)).

# Limits and Defaults

This page collects the fixed limits and the defaults you can meet in Sodero Cloud, each with the page that explains it. Your workspace's plan sets further limits, such as storage and how many Robot Systems and Robot Worlds can be active at once: **Billing & Usage** shows them ([Set by Your Plan](#set-by-your-plan)).

______________________________________________________________________

## Names

| What                                             | Limit                                                                                                                                                            | More                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Workspace name                                   | Up to 30 characters                                                                                                                                              | [Workspaces and People](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/workspaces/index.md)               |
| Project name and description                     | Name up to 20 characters, description up to 40                                                                                                                   | [Projects](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/projects/#2-create-a-project)                  |
| Robot System or Robot World name and description | File name up to 20 characters, description up to 40                                                                                                              | [Robot Systems and Robot Worlds](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/files/#1-create-a-file)  |
| Node name in a Station                           | Up to 60 characters; 20 for an empty draft such as **Empty gateway**. Letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, starting with a letter or digit. Unique in the Station. | [Build the Graph](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/graph/#name-the-node)                    |
| Robot name of a simulation gateway               | Exactly the robot's articulation prim name in the World: up to 64 characters, letters, digits and `_`, not starting with a digit. Unique in the World.           | [Connect to the World](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/world_connection/#2-name-the-robot) |
| Password                                         | At least 8 characters                                                                                                                                            | [Sign In and Account](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/sign_in/index.md)                    |

______________________________________________________________________

## Projects, Files and Runs

| What                                    | Limit or default                                                                                                                                                | More                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Active Robot Worlds per project         | 1                                                                                                                                                               | [Robot Systems and Robot Worlds](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/files/#4-how-robot-worlds-and-robot-systems-work-together) |
| Active Robot Systems per project        | Any number, within your plan's limit of **Systems and Worlds running at once**                                                                                  | [Billing and Usage](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/billing/#limits)                                                         |
| Auto off                                | Deactivates an active Robot System or Robot World after 30 minutes without users (the default). On by default.                                                  | [Auto Off](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#5-auto-off)                                                        |
| Files in one **Actions** selection      | Any number of Robot Systems, at most one Robot World                                                                                                            | [Several Files at Once](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/#4-several-files-at-once)                              |
| Nodes after **Activate** or **Go live** | No node starts by itself                                                                                                                                        | [Start and Monitor Nodes](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/run/index.md)                                                      |
| Station resources                       | Each Station gets its own share of CPU and memory from Sodero Cloud. **Resources** in the Station and the **Resource** column of the project page show its use. | [Stellar Station](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/overview/#4-resources)                                                     |
| Node logs in the Station                | The last 200 lines of each stream                                                                                                                               | [Logs and Activity](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/run/#5-logs-and-activity)                                                |

______________________________________________________________________

## Files and Uploads

| What                           | Limit                                                                                                      | More                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A file in a library            | Up to 2 GiB                                                                                                | [Libraries](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/libraries/#2-add-files) |
| An upload in Studio            | Up to 1 GiB per file                                                                                       | [Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/studio/index.md)             |
| A file uploaded by an AI agent | Up to 1 GiB for a library file; up to 64 MiB for any other upload, such as a Station document or a package | [AI Agents](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/ai_agents/#usage-limits) |

______________________________________________________________________

## Sharing and Connections

| What                               | Limit                                              | More                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Project or workspace invitation    | Valid for 7 days                                   | [Share and Collaborate](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/sharing/#1-invite-people) |
| Project VPN connections            | 3 open connections per person, across all projects | [Project VPN](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/project_vpn/#limits)                 |
| Length of a Project VPN connection | At most 8 hours                                    | [Project VPN](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/project_vpn/#limits)                 |
| AI agent connection                | Up to 30 days, then sign the agent in again        | [AI Agents](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/ai_agents/#usage-limits)               |
| AI agent tool call                 | Ends after 100 seconds                             | [AI Agents](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/ai_agents/#usage-limits)               |

______________________________________________________________________

## Set by Your Plan

Your workspace's plan sets these limits. **Billing & Usage**, in the workspace menu, shows each one with what the workspace uses ([Billing and Usage](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/billing/index.md)):

- credits, their hourly rates and when they renew;
- **Projects** in the workspace;
- **Workspace storage** and **Project libraries**;
- **Systems and Worlds running at once**;
- **AI agent (MCP) tool calls**, **Project VPN time** and **Project VPN data** per calendar month;
- AI agent tool calls per minute, when the plan limits them (*Agents can make up to N tool calls per minute.*).

Plans differ, so this manual gives no values for them. To change the plan or add credits, contact Sodero.

2026.10.30

## v1.0.0

#### Release

- **Get started.** What Sodero Cloud is, its key concepts, and a [Quick Start](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/get_started/quick_start/index.md) that creates, runs and stops a Robot World. Example files to connect a Robot System to it.
- **Account, workspaces and projects.** [Sign-in](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/sign_in/index.md), [workspaces and people](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/workspaces/index.md), [billing and usage](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/account/billing/index.md), [projects](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/projects/index.md), [Robot Systems and Robot Worlds](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/files/index.md), [activation](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/activate_run/index.md), [libraries](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/libraries/index.md) and [sharing](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/projects/sharing/index.md).
- **Worlds.** Build a Robot World in [Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/studio/index.md), [prepare it for simulation](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/prepare_world/index.md) and watch it run in [Theater](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/worlds/theater/index.md).
- **Robot Systems.** Configure [Stellar Station](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/station/overview/index.md) in the cloud: apps and packages, the node graph, documents and settings, the connection to the World, and running nodes.
- **Operate robots.** [Strider](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/strider/index.md), [Motion Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/motion_studio/index.md) and [Articulation](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/operate/articulation/index.md) with robots in a Robot World.
- **Connect and automate.** The [Project VPN](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/project_vpn/index.md) and [AI agents](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/connect/ai_agents/index.md).
- **Reference.** [Compatibility](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/reference/compatibility/index.md) and [Limits and Defaults](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/v1.0.0/reference/limits/index.md).
